definition_zh: 心态；思维方式；智力水平
definition_en: the typical way of thinking of a person or group, or a person general level of intelligence
core_image: 一副眼镜架在鼻梁上，镜片把同一件事染成不同的颜色
scene: 两个同学面对一次失败的考试：一个说下次再来，一个说反正我不行。Two classmates failed the test, yet they showed a completely different mentality about it.
sceneCN: 这里 mentality 是「心态；思维方式」（第 1 个义项：一个群体或一个人习惯性的思考方式）；句意：两个同学都没考好，但他们对这件事的态度截然不同。

pos.zh: 心态；思维方式；智力水平

collocations.zh: 背水一战的心态；受困心态

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 mens 加 -al 构成，义为「精神的；心理的」，是 mentality 的直接基础
由 mental 加 -ly 构成，义为「精神上；在心理上」
由拉丁语词根 ment 加 -ation 构成，义为「心理活动；思维过程」，常用于心理学

senses.title: A characteristic way of thinking
senses.definition: the habitual way in which a person or group thinks about things
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体看待事物的习惯性方式
senses.example: The new staff brought a positive mentality to the team.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工给团队带来了积极的心态。
senses.why: The Latin root mens means mind, and the -ity ending turns mind into a fixed frame through which things are seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 mens 意为「心、精神」，后缀 -ity 把它固定成一副看世界的框架，这就是思维方式。

senses.title: Mindsets shared by a group
senses.definition: the collective outlook of a community, a profession, or a generation
senses.definitionCN: 某个社群、行业或一代人共有的观念与态度
senses.example: Scholars have studied the siege mentality of isolated communities.
senses.exampleCN: 学者研究过孤立群体的受困心态。
senses.why: A frame of mind is not private, so when many minds share one frame the word widens from a person to a group.
senses.whyCN: 看世界的框架并不只属于个人，当许多头脑共用一副框架时，这个词就从个人扩展到群体。

senses.title: A person level of intelligence
senses.definition: the natural or developed ability of a person to think and learn, often used approvingly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人思考和学习的自然或习得能力，常带赞许语气
senses.example: She has the mentality to master three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她有掌握三门语言的头脑。
senses.why: If mens is the mind itself, the -ity noun can name the power of that mind rather than its habits.
senses.whyCN: 如果 mens 指的是心智本身，那么 -ity 名词也可以指这股心智的能力，而不只是它的习惯。

senses.title: A narrow or limited outlook
senses.definition: a way of thinking seen as rigid, narrow, or fixed by habit
senses.definitionCN: 被视为僵硬、狭隘或被习惯固定的思维方式
senses.example: Critics attacked the mentality that prizes exams above curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击那种把考试看得比好奇心更重要的思维定式。
senses.why: A settled frame is efficient, but once a frame decides everything it turns into a limitation, a closed view.
senses.whyCN: 固定的框架很好用，可一旦这副框架替人决定了一切，它就变成了限制，成为封闭的视角。

senses.title: A short-lived frame of mind
senses.definition: a particular mood or attitude held at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 在特定时刻持有的情绪或态度
senses.example: The holiday mentality of office workers fades by Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 上班族的假日心态一到周一就消失了。
senses.why: The same frame can slip on for a day and off again, so the noun also names a passing way of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 同一副心态框架可以只戴一天就摘下，所以这个词也指一种暂时的心情。

intro.en: Mentality comes from mental, which descends from Latin mens, mind, and from the Latin noun formations in -itas, which English turns into -ity.
intro.cn: mentality 来自 mental，而 mental 出自拉丁语 mens（心、精神），再加拉丁语 -itas 类名词后缀，英语作 -ity。

items.en: Mens means the mind, the intellect, or a settled way of feeling; from it come mentalis and the poetical ment- forms.
items.cn: mens 意为心、理智或固定的感受方式，由此产生 mentalis 等形容词形式。

items.en: Noun formation with -itas, as in qualitas and utilitas, turns an adjective into an abstract quality.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语用 -itas 把形容词变成抽象名词，如 qualitas、utilitas。

items.en: Mental enters English from the Latin adjective mentalis, meaning of the mind.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入 mental，源自拉丁语形容词 mentalis，意为「心智的」。

items.en: Mentality is formed in the seventeenth century as mental plus -ity, first naming mental powers or the state of mind.
items.cn: 十七世纪由 mental 加 -ity 构成 mentality，最初指心智能力或精神状态。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word spreads to whole nations, classes, and professions and comes to mean their collective outlook.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，这个词扩展到国家、阶层与行业，指它们共有的观念。

note.en: Mentality is the mind-shaped noun beside mental, and in meaning it stands close to mindset, outlook, and attitude.
note.cn: mentality 是与 mental 相邻、由「心智」构成的名词，意义上靠近 mindset、outlook 与 attitude。

entries.definition: relating to the mind
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词根构成，义为「精神的；心理的」

entries.definition: in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 与目标词同族，是副词，义为「在精神上」

entries.definition: explaining behaviour by mental states
entries.definitionCN: 与目标词同出拉丁语 mens，是学术形容词，义为「用心理状态解释行为的」

entries.definition: a fixed set of opinions or habits of mind
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指固定的看法或思维习惯，多用于现代心理学与商业

entries.definition: a person general attitude to life
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指对生活的一般看法与态度

entries.definition: a settled way of feeling about something
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指对某事稳定的看法与感受

normalIntro.en: Mentality is made of mens, mind, plus -ity, the ending that turns a word into a quality, so it is literally the quality of a mind.
normalIntro.cn: mentality 由 mens（心）加 -ity（构成性质名词的后缀）组成，字面意思就是「心智的性质」。

normal.en: The family of words runs from mental through mentality to mentally.
normal.cn: 这一族词从 mental 到 mentality 再到 mentally，一路延伸。

normal.en: A siege mentality describes feeling surrounded, as in the phrase a siege mentality.
normal.cn: siege mentality 形容觉得自己被围困的心态。

normal.en: Herd mentality means following the crowd without thinking.
normal.cn: herd mentality 指不加思考地随大流。

normal.en: Compare mindset: mindset is the modern equivalent, mentality is more often critical in tone.
normal.cn: 对比 mindset：mindset 是现代对等说法，mentality 常带批评色彩。

normal.en: The plural is mentalities, as in the mentalities of two generations.
normal.cn: 复数是 mentalities，例如两代人的不同心态。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of glasses that colours everything on the nose of the wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一副眼镜戴在鼻梁上，把眼前一切染成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole crowd wearing the same pair of glasses.
abstract.cn: 想象一整个人群戴着同一副眼镜。

abstract.en: Think of a ruler marking out how far a mind can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在量一颗头脑能伸多远。

examples.en: The old mentality of saving every penny dies hard.
examples.cn: 那种一分一厘都要攒下的旧心态很难改变。

examples.en: National mentalities change slowly after a long war.
examples.cn: 长期战乱之后，民族心态变化得很慢。

examples.en: The coach praised the players for their winning mentality.
examples.cn: 教练称赞了球员们的必胜心态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门探逻辑」——一个人进门先探一探这里讲的是什么逻辑，这种习惯就是他的思维方式；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mens（心、精神）→ mentalis（心智的）→ 英语 mental（精神的）→ mental + -ity → mentality，核心义「心智呈现出的性质，即看世界的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Mentality runs from an individual habit of mind, to a shared outlook, to the power of the mind, to a narrow fixed view, and finally to a passing mood.
sensesIntro.cn: mentality 从个人看世界的习惯，到群体共有的观念，再到头脑本身的能力，再到狭隘僵化的视角，最后到一时的心境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of glasses that colours everything the wearer sees.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副把所见之物都染成同色的眼镜。

branches.en: One person wearing the glasses is the individual habit of mind.
branches.cn: 一个人戴着眼镜，就是个人看世界的习惯。

branches.en: Many people sharing the same glasses gives the group sense.
branches.cn: 许多人共用一副眼镜，就引出群体心态。

branches.en: The lens itself, rather than its tint, is the mind power sense.
branches.cn: 镜片本身而非它的颜色，对应头脑能力的义项。

branches.en: Glasses that cannot be taken off become a narrow fixed view.
branches.cn: 摘不下来的眼镜，就成了狭隘僵化的视角。

branches.en: A shared frame can last a generation or only a day.
branches.cn: 同一副框架可以延续一代人，也可以只维持一天。

intro.en: Mentality is built on the Latin mind root mens, with the adjective mental and the abstract noun ending -ity around it.
intro.cn: mentality 建立在拉丁语表示「心」的词根 mens 之上，周围有形容词 mental 与抽象名词后缀 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin mens is the mind, mentalis means mental, and -itas is the late Latin suffix for a quality, which English changed to -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心，mentalis 意为心智的，-itas 是晚期拉丁语表示性质的后缀，英语作 -ity。

items.example: Mens supplies the core of the word.
items.exampleCN: mens 提供这个词的核心。

items.example: Mentalis gives English mental.
items.exampleCN: mentalis 给出英语 mental。

items.example: The Latin suffix -itas gives English -ity.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁后缀 -itas 对应英语 -ity。

items.example: Mental enters English in the fifteenth century.
items.exampleCN: mental 在十五世纪进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 构成抽象性质名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms mentality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 mentality。

items.example: The noun names a frame of mind.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指一种看世界的框架。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mentally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 mentally。

items.example: Mentally is the adverb of the family.
items.exampleCN: mentally 是这一族词中的副词。

items.meaningCN: 以 y 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The ending -ies gives mentalities.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ies 构成复数 mentalities。

definition_zh: 导师；顾问；辅导；指导
definition_en: an experienced person who advises and helps a less experienced one, or to act in that role
core_image: 一位长者把手搭在年轻人肩上，指着前方的路
scene: 实验室里，老教授每周都抽时间帮新博士生改论文、理思路。The old professor meets the new PhD student every week to mentor her through her first paper.
sceneCN: 这里 mentor 是动词「指导；辅导」（第 4 个义项：以导师身份长期帮助某人）；句意：老教授每周都与这位新博士生见面，指导她写完第一篇论文。

collocations.zh: 指导某人度过某个过程

derivatives.zh: 由 mentor 加 -ship 构成，义为「导师身份；指导关系」
由 mentor 加 -ing 构成，义为「指导；师徒带教」，也可作形容词
由 mentor 加 -ee 构成，义为「受指导者；学员」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「有人指导的」

senses.title: An experienced adviser
senses.definition: a person with more experience who advises and guides someone with less
senses.definitionCN: 经验更丰富、给经验较少者建议和指引的人
senses.example: She became a mentor to every new intern in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了实验室里每位新实习生的导师。
senses.why: The name begins with the wise old friend in Homer, so a mentor is first a person whose experience is lent to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于荷马笔下那位年长而智慧的朋友，所以 mentor 首先是一个把自己的经验借给别人的人。

senses.title: A trusted counsellor at work
senses.definition: a colleague or senior figure whose advice shapes another person career
senses.definitionCN: 为他人职业发展提供指引的同事或前辈
senses.example: My first manager was a mentor for more than twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 我的第一任经理当了我二十多年的良师。
senses.why: Because guidance is a relationship rather than a job title, the mentor sense spreads into work and career.
senses.whyCN: 因为指导是一种关系而不是职位头衔，所以导师义自然延伸到工作与职业领域。

senses.title: A model of conduct
senses.definition: a person whose example others follow, even without formal advice
senses.definitionCN: 即便不给正式建议，他人也会效法其言行的人
senses.example: Her quiet courage made her a mentor to the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 她无声的勇气让全村人都以她为榜样。
senses.why: The person who guides by walking ahead does not need to speak, so the mentor can be an example rather than an adviser.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的人不必开口也能带路，所以 mentor 可以只是一个榜样，而不必给建议。

senses.title: To guide someone
senses.definition: to advise and help a learner over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里指导并帮助学习者
senses.example: Senior engineers mentor the graduates through their first project.
senses.exampleCN: 资深工程师带着毕业生完成第一个项目。
senses.why: Once the hand on the shoulder becomes an action, the word works as a verb meaning to lend experience over time.
senses.whyCN: 当搭在肩上的那只手变成一个动作，这个词就作动词用，表示长期地把经验借给别人。

senses.title: A wise voice in literature
senses.definition: a character who secretly guides the hero and helps the hero grow
senses.definitionCN: 暗中引导主角、助其成长的文学角色
senses.example: Critics call the old sailor the mentor of the young narrator.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称那位老水手是年轻叙述者的引导者。
senses.why: The original mentor was a disguised goddess, so the word keeps a literary sense of a guiding presence behind the scenes.
senses.whyCN: 最初的 mentor 是乔装的女神，因此这个词保留了暗处引导者的文学含义。

intro.en: Mentor is a proper name taken from Greek, the name of the old friend whom Odysseus left in charge of his household in the Odyssey.
intro.cn: mentor 直接取自希腊语人名，即《奥德赛》中奥德修斯托付家事的旧友之名。

items.en: Greek Mentōr is the name of a trusted friend of Odysseus, and of the form in which the goddess Athena advises Telemachus.
items.cn: 希腊语 Mentōr 是奥德修斯信任的友人之名，女神雅典娜也化作这个形象指点忒勒马科斯。

items.en: Roman writers keep the name Mentor unchanged when retelling the story.
items.cn: 罗马作家重述这一故事时原样保留了 Mentor 这个名字。

items.en: In the 1740s English moralists published essays under the pen name Mentor, reviving the word as a type name.
items.cn: 十八世纪四十年代，英国道德作家以 Mentor 为笔名发表文章，使这个词重新作为类型名使用。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century a mentor is any wise guide, and by the twentieth century the word takes a verb use.
items.cn: 自十八世纪末起，mentor 泛指任何明智的引路人；到二十世纪又获得动词用法。

items.en: Today mentoring is an organised part of schools, firms, and professions, and mentorship names the relationship itself.
items.cn: 今天师徒指导已成为学校、企业与行业的制度化安排，mentorship 则指这种关系本身。

note.en: Mentor is a name turned into a common noun, related by form to mentorship and mentee and by meaning to coach, tutor, and adviser.
note.cn: mentor 本是专名，后转为普通名词，形式上与 mentorship、mentee 相邻，意义上与 coach、tutor、adviser 相邻。

entries.definition: the role or relationship of a mentor
entries.definitionCN: 由 mentor 加 -ship 构成，义为「导师身份；指导关系」

entries.definition: a person who is guided by a mentor
entries.definitionCN: 由 mentor 加 -ee 构成，义为「受指导者」，是导师的另一端

entries.definition: relating to the mind, with a similar opening
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同，义为「精神的；心理的」

entries.definition: a person who trains others in a skill or performance
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指训练他人技能或表现的人，偏重训练与激励

entries.definition: a teacher who gives individual lessons
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指一对一个别授课的教师，偏重学业

entries.definition: a person who gives expert advice
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指提供专业建议的人，不一定长期陪伴

normalIntro.en: Mentor is a name from Homer that became a common noun for the older hand on a younger shoulder.
normalIntro.cn: mentor 是出自荷马的一个名字，后来变成普通名词，指搭在年轻人肩上的那只年长的手。

normal.en: The Homeric name Mentor belonged to the old friend who guarded Odysseus and his son.
normal.cn: 荷马故事里的 Mentor 是守护奥德修斯父子多年的老友。

normal.en: Mentorship names the relationship, and mentee names the person being guided.
normal.cn: mentorship 指这种关系，mentee 指被指导的一方。

normal.en: Mentor works as a verb meaning to guide, as in mentoring a new colleague.
normal.cn: mentor 也可以作动词，表示指导，如辅导新同事。

normal.en: Compare coach: a coach trains a skill, while a mentor shapes a person over time.
normal.cn: 对比 coach：coach 训练技能，mentor 则在长时间里塑造一个人。

normal.en: The pair mentor and mentee mirrors trainer and trainee.
normal.cn: mentor 与 mentee 的配对，就像 trainer 与 trainee。

abstract.en: Picture an old hand resting on a young shoulder, pointing forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一只年长的手搭在年轻肩头，指向前方。

abstract.en: Think of a whole office walking behind one pair of steady shoulders.
abstract.cn: 想象一整个办公室的人跟在一双稳健的肩膀后面走。

abstract.en: See a torch passed from an older hand to a younger one.
abstract.cn: 想象一支火炬从年长的手中传到年轻的手中。

examples.en: A good mentor asks questions rather than giving answers.
examples.cn: 好的导师多问问题，少给答案。

examples.en: She mentored three young researchers last year.
examples.cn: 她去年指导了三名年轻研究人员。

examples.en: The firm offers mentorship to all new employees.
examples.cn: 公司为所有新员工提供导师辅导。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门徒」——把门收下当徒弟，带他进门的人就是导师；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语人名 Mentōr（奥德修斯的忠实老友，后由雅典娜化身指点其子）→ 拉丁语沿用 → 现代英语普通名词 mentor（导师），核心义「领路的长者」。

sensesIntro.en: Mentor begins as the experienced person who advises, widens to a career counsellor and a living model, then becomes a verb, and finally keeps a literary sense of the hidden guide.
sensesIntro.cn: mentor 最初指给出建议的经历丰富者，后扩展到职业顾问与活榜样，再转为动词，最后保留了文学中「暗处引导者」的含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an older hand resting on a younger shoulder and pointing the way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只年长的手搭在年轻人肩上，为他指路。

branches.en: The experienced person who lends counsel keeps the classical name most closely.
branches.cn: 把经验和建议借给别人的那个人，最贴近古典名字的本义。

branches.en: The guides at work narrow the word to career and profession.
branches.cn: 职场上的引路人把词义收窄到职业与行业。

branches.en: A model needs no advice because walking ahead is itself the guidance.
branches.cn: 榜样不必开口，因为走在前面本身就是指引。

branches.en: The hand on the shoulder becomes an action in the verb.
branches.cn: 搭在肩上的手在动词里化成了一个动作。

branches.en: The literary hidden helper and the everyday adviser share one guiding presence.
branches.cn: 文学中暗处的引导者与日常的顾问共享同一种引路角色。

intro.en: Mentor is a proper name turned into a word, and English has built mentorship, mentoring, and mentee around it without any inherited root.
intro.cn: mentor 是由专名转化而来的词，英语围绕它造出 mentorship、mentoring 与 mentee，它本身没有承袭的词根。

latinIntro.en: The name passes through Latin unchanged from Greek Mentōr; no Latin root underlies it, and Greek mentōr itself has an uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名字经拉丁语原样传下，源出希腊语 Mentōr；它没有拉丁词根，而希腊语 mentōr 本身的来源也不确定。

items.meaning: the trusted friend in the Odyssey
items.example: Mentōr gives the word its classical image.
items.exampleCN: Mentōr 提供这个词的古典意象。

items.meaning: a pen name used by moralists, and the literary guide
items.meaningCN: 道德作家用过的笔名，也指文学中的引导者
items.example: The pen name Mentor revived the word in the 1740s.
items.exampleCN: 笔名 Mentor 在十八世纪四十年代复活了这个词。

items.example: The common noun keeps the guiding role.
items.exampleCN: 普通名词保留引路者的含义。

items.example: The verb describes the ongoing act of guiding.
items.exampleCN: 动词描述持续进行的指导行为。

items.meaning: forming a noun of state or relationship
items.meaningCN: 构成状态或关系名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ship forms mentorship.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ship 构成 mentorship。

items.example: Mentorship names the relationship itself.
items.exampleCN: mentorship 指这种关系本身。

items.meaning: a person who receives an action
items.meaningCN: 承受某动作的人的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ee forms mentee.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ee 构成 mentee。

items.example: Mentee is the other end of the relationship.
items.exampleCN: mentee 是这种关系的另一端。

items.meaning: forming a noun or adjective from a verb
items.meaningCN: 由动词构成名词或形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms mentoring.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 mentoring。

items.example: Mentoring is now part of staff training.
items.exampleCN: 师徒带教如今是员工培训的一部分。

definition_zh: 合并；并入；融合；使渐渐消失
definition_en: to join together so as to form a single thing, or to become part of something larger
core_image: 两条支流在水口撞在一起，拧成一条更宽的河
scene: 两条乡间小路在一座旧桥下面合成一条大路，来往的车流从此走得更顺。The two country lanes merge under an old bridge, and the traffic flows more smoothly.
sceneCN: 这里 merge 是「合并、汇入」（第 1 个义项：两股合成一股）；句意：两条乡间小路在一座旧桥下面合成一条大路，来往的车流从此走得更顺。

pos.zh: 合并；融合；并入；使渐渐消失

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「合并；并购」
由现在分词名词化而来，义为「合并过程」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「已合并的」
同出拉丁词根，意为「浮现；出现」

senses.title: To flow together into one
senses.definition: of roads, streams, or lines, to join and become one
senses.definitionCN: 道路、水流或线条相接并成为一条
senses.example: The two rivers merge below the town.
senses.exampleCN: 两条河在镇子下游汇合。
senses.why: The Latin word mergere means to dip or plunge into, so two things dive into each other and come out as one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mergere 意为「浸入、没入」，两样东西一旦互相没入，就合成了一个。

senses.title: To combine organizations
senses.definition: of companies or groups, to unite into a single organization
senses.definitionCN: 公司或团体合并成一个组织
senses.example: The two banks merged last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家银行去年春天合并了。
senses.why: Once two flows become one stream, the image easily moves to two firms becoming one firm.
senses.whyCN: 两股水合成一股的画面很容易移到两家公司合成一家上。

senses.title: To blend into a whole
senses.definition: to mix so that separate parts can no longer be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 混合到分不清原来各部分的程度
senses.example: Her voice merged with the sound of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音融入了人群的喧闹。
senses.why: Immersing things in one another blurs their edges, so merging also means blending indistinguishably.
senses.whyCN: 彼此浸没会让边界变模糊，所以 merge 也指融合得难分彼此。

senses.title: To fade into a background
senses.definition: to become lost in or disappear gradually into something around it
senses.definitionCN: 渐渐隐没在周围的环境里
senses.example: The dark car merged into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆深色的车消失在夜色里。
senses.why: Dip something into a liquid and it vanishes, so fading into a background keeps the plunging image.
senses.whyCN: 把东西浸进液体就看不见了，所以「隐入背景」仍然沿用没入的画面。

senses.title: A uniting of things
senses.definition: the act or result of joining two or more things into one
senses.definitionCN: 两样或更多事物合成一样的行为或结果
senses.example: The merge of the two files took a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 合并这两个文件只用了一会儿。
senses.why: The verb easily turns into a noun naming the joining itself, common in business and computing.
senses.whyCN: 动词很容易转成名词，用来指合并这件事本身，在商业和计算机领域很常用。

senses.title: To blend traffic lanes
senses.definition: of vehicles, to move into a lane where other traffic is already flowing
senses.definitionCN: 车辆驶入已有车流的车道
senses.example: The sign tells drivers to merge.
senses.exampleCN: 路标提示司机向左并道。
senses.why: A car sliding into a lane copies a stream entering a larger stream.
senses.whyCN: 车滑进另一条车道，正如一条小流汇入大流。

intro.en: Merge comes from Latin mergere, to dip or plunge into, probably through French merger.
intro.cn: merge 来自拉丁语 mergere（浸入、没入），一般认为经由法语 merger 进入英语。

items.en: Mergere means to dip or plunge something into liquid.
items.cn: mergere 意为把东西浸入、没入液体。

items.en: The Latin past participle mersus gives words like immersus, dipped in.
items.cn: 拉丁语过去分词 mersus 衍生出 immersus（浸入的）等词。

items.en: Generally it passed through French merger with the sense of plunging.
items.cn: 一般认为它经由法语 merger（俯冲、没入）的中介。

items.en: English merge first meant to sink or be swallowed up.
items.cn: 英语 merge 最初表示沉没或被吞没。

items.en: The legal sense of joining rights or estates grew into business and computing merges.
items.cn: 法律上「权利或财产归并」的用法后来扩展为商业与计算机的合并。

note.en: Merge belongs to the Latin family of dip or plunge, and sits beside words for uniting two flows.
note.cn: merge 属于拉丁语「浸入」词族，语义上与表示两股合流的词相邻。

entries.definition: the joining of two companies into one
entries.definitionCN: 由 merge 加 -er 构成，指两家公司合成一家

entries.definition: to come out into view
entries.definitionCN: 与 merge 同出拉丁语 mergere，前缀 e- 表示「向外」，义为浮现

entries.definition: to put under water
entries.definitionCN: 前缀 sub- 表示「在下」，动词意为使没入水中

entries.definition: to join two or more things together
entries.definitionCN: 把两样或更多事物结合起来

entries.definition: to join by melting into one mass
to combine organizations into one

normalIntro.en: Merge is a plunging word: things dip into each other and come out as one.
normalIntro.cn: merge 是「没入」的词：东西互相浸进去，出来时已经是一体。

normal.en: Merge with means to join another thing.
normal.cn: merge with 表示与另一事物合并。

normal.en: The noun merger is the standard business word for a takeover.
normal.cn: 名词 merger 是商业里「并购」的标准说法。

normal.en: Submerge keeps the same root and means to go under water.
normal.cn: submerge 保留同一词根，意为没入水中。

normal.en: Emerge reverses the prefix and means to come out.
normal.cn: emerge 换了前缀，意为露出来。

normal.en: In traffic, a sign may tell drivers to merge, meaning to slide into the next lane.
normal.cn: 交通标志上写「向左并道」，指滑进左侧车道。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting in a single channel.
abstract.cn: 想象两条小溪在同一个沟槽里相会。

abstract.en: Picture two logos on one letterhead after a deal.
abstract.cn: 想象一桩交易之后，一张信纸上并排印着两个标志。

abstract.en: Picture paint of two colours stirred until no seam remains.
abstract.cn: 想象两团颜料被搅到再也看不出接缝。

examples.en: The government plans to merge the two agencies next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年把这两个机构合并。

examples.en: After the rain the stream merged with the main river.
examples.cn: 雨后小溪汇入了主河道。

examples.en: Keep your files separate until you merge them.
examples.cn: 合并文件之前，先让它们各自分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸之」——两样东西摸着摸着就合到了一起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mergere（浸入、没入）→ 一般认为经法语 merger → 英语 merge，核心义「各自没入，合成一体」。

sensesIntro.en: Merge starts with streams flowing into one, then moves to companies uniting, to things blending, to fading away, and finally to the noun for the joining itself.
sensesIntro.cn: merge 先指水流合成一股，再指公司合并、事物融合、渐渐隐没，最后名词化指合并本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two streams plunging into the same channel.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条水流没入同一条河道。

branches.en: Physical streams and roads are the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 水流与道路的汇合是具体义项。

branches.en: Companies uniting is the organizational sense.
branches.cn: 公司合并是组织义项。

branches.en: Blending into a whole is the mixing sense.
branches.cn: 融合成一体是混合义项。

branches.en: Fading away comes from being swallowed by surroundings.
branches.cn: 隐没是从被环境吞没的画面延伸出来的。

branches.en: The noun merge and traffic merging both name a joining movement.
branches.cn: 名词 merge 与并道都是「汇入」这一动作的名词化或具体化。

intro.en: Merge is a borrowing from Latin mergere, with a family of em-, sub-, and de- forms.
intro.cn: merge 借自拉丁语 mergere，英语中围绕它有 em-、sub-、de- 等一套形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin mergere means to dip or plunge, and its past participle mersus gives many English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mergere 意为浸入、没入，其过去分词 mersus 衍生出许多英语词。

items.example: The root merg- supplies the plunging image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 merg- 提供没入的意象。

items.example: Mergere is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: mergere 是来源动词。

items.example: Merge is the borrowed verb.
items.exampleCN: merge 是借来的动词。

items.example: Emerge means rise out of the liquid.
items.exampleCN: emerge 意为从液体里升出来。

items.example: Submerge puts the thing beneath the surface.
items.exampleCN: submerge 把东西置于水面之下。

items.example: The suffix -er forms merger and emerger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 merger 与 emerger。

items.example: Merger is the standard business noun.
items.exampleCN: merger 是商业里的标准名词。

items.example: The suffix -ent forms emergent and submergent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 构成 emergent 与 submergent。

items.meaning: to put fully into a liquid
items.example: Immerse uses the same past participle stem.
items.exampleCN: immerse 用的是同一个过去分词词干。

items.example: Merged is used as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: merged 可用作形容词。

definition_zh: 网眼；网；网格；网状物；啮合；协调一致
definition_en: a material made of threads or wires woven into a net with small regular holes, or to fit closely together
core_image: 细线来回穿梭，织成一张方格整齐的网
scene: 渔夫把一张尼龙网撒进浅湾，网眼在晨光里闪着细密的方格。The fisherman cast a nylon mesh into the shallow bay, its small squares shining in the morning light.
sceneCN: 这里 mesh 是「网」（第 1 个义项：由线或丝编成的网）；句意：渔夫把一张尼龙网撒进浅湾，网眼在晨光里闪着细密的方格。

pos.zh: 网；网状物；网眼；网格；啮合
啮合；紧密配合；协调一致

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「网状的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「拆开网；使脱离啮合」
由 mesh 加 work 构成，义为「网状结构」
由现在分词名词化而来，义为「啮合；咬合过程」

senses.title: A net of small holes
senses.definition: a material of threads or wires woven with small regular holes
senses.definitionCN: 用线或金属丝编成、带规则小孔的网材
senses.example: The window is covered with fine mesh.
senses.exampleCN: 窗户上罩着细网。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is simply a net, and the word still pictures woven square holes.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是一张网，这个词至今仍带着方正网眼的画面。

senses.title: A single hole in a net
senses.definition: one of the small openings between the threads of a net or sieve
senses.definitionCN: 网或筛子上两条线之间的一个小孔
senses.example: The fish is too small for the mesh.
senses.exampleCN: 这条鱼太小，能从网眼里溜走。
senses.why: The whole net and one of its holes share a name, so mesh shifts from the material to the opening.
senses.whyCN: 整张网和单个孔共用同一个词，所以 mesh 可以从网材转到孔上。

senses.title: The point where gears fit
senses.definition: the state in which teeth of wheels or parts interlock
senses.definitionCN: 齿轮或部件彼此咬合的状态
senses.example: The gears are out of mesh.
senses.exampleCN: 齿轮没有咬合上。
senses.why: A net is where lines cross and hold, so two sets of teeth meeting like crossed threads also mesh.
senses.whyCN: 网是线交叉互锁的地方，两组齿像线一样咬合，也就叫 mesh。

senses.title: To interlock mechanically
senses.definition: of wheels or parts, to fit together and move as one
senses.definitionCN: 轮子或部件互相咬合，一起转动
senses.example: The teeth of the two wheels mesh smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 两个轮子的齿咬合得很顺。
senses.why: The noun sense of interlocking easily becomes a verb of the same action.
senses.whyCN: 名词里「咬合」的含义很容易转成同一动作的动词。

senses.title: To fit well together
senses.definition: of plans, ideas, or people, to be in harmony with each other
senses.definitionCN: 计划、想法或人彼此和谐配合
senses.example: Her story meshes with the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说法和事实吻合。
senses.why: When teeth fit, the machine runs, so things that combine neatly are said to mesh.
senses.whyCN: 齿一咬上，机器就转得顺，于是「配合得当」也用 mesh。

senses.title: A netting for protection
senses.definition: a light netting used to keep insects out or guard a surface
senses.definitionCN: 用来挡虫或护住表面的轻质网
senses.example: The builders fitted a safety mesh beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在路边装了安全网。
senses.why: Woven openings let air through while holding small things back, a natural job for the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 编织的孔既能透气又能挡住小东西，这正是网的天然用途。

intro.en: Mesh comes from Middle Dutch or Low German maesche, a net opening, related to the same Germanic root as English net words for meshes.
intro.cn: mesh 来自中古荷兰语或低地德语 maesche（网眼），一般认为与日耳曼语系表示网眼的词根同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root mesh word meant the opening in a net.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语中有一个表示网眼的重构词根。

items.en: Maesche names one hole of a netting.
items.cn: maesche 指网编物上的一个孔洞。

items.en: Medieval English adopted the word for a net opening.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个词，指网眼。

items.en: The noun spreads from one opening to the whole woven net.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，名词由单个孔洞扩展到整张网。

items.en: Engineering adds the gear senses, and modern usage adds fitting together well.
items.cn: 工程领域增加了齿轮啮合的用法，现代又增加了配合一致的含义。

note.en: Mesh is a small Germanic word for net openings, close to net and grid words and to terms of fitting together.
note.cn: mesh 是表示网眼的日耳曼语小词，与 net、grid 一类词以及表示契合的词相邻。

entries.definition: more than one net or mesh
entries.definitionCN: mesh 的复数或三单形式

entries.definition: fitted together or caught in a net
entries.definitionCN: mesh 的过去式，指咬合上或被网住

entries.definition: a structure of interlaced lines
entries.definitionCN: 由 mesh 与 work 复合而成，指网状结构

entries.definition: a material of knotted cord with holes
a set of crossing bars forming squares
entries.definitionCN: 交叉成方格的格栅或网格

entries.definition: to fit together closely

normalIntro.en: Mesh is woven squares that hold things and also gear teeth that lock into them.
normalIntro.cn: mesh 既是锁住东西的方格网，也是咬成网状的齿轮齿。

normal.en: Wire mesh is used for fences.
normal.cn: wire mesh 即铁丝网，常用来做围栏。

normal.en: To mesh with something means to fit it well.
normal.cn: mesh with 某物，意思与它配合得好。

normal.en: Mesh size tells you how wide the holes are.
normal.cn: mesh size 指网眼有多大。

normal.en: In engineering, gears mesh when their teeth engage.
normal.cn: 工程上，齿轮齿一咬上就叫啮合。

normal.en: Compare net: a net is knotted rope, while mesh can be any woven sheet of openings.
normal.cn: 对比 net：net 是打结的绳网，而 mesh 可以是任何编织成的带孔薄片。

abstract.en: Picture a fishing net spread out on the deck.
abstract.cn: 想象一张渔网摊在甲板上。

abstract.en: Picture two cogwheels turning without slipping.
abstract.cn: 想象两个齿轮咬合转动而不打滑。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces clicking into place.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图咔一声嵌在一起。

examples.en: The screen door has a fine steel mesh.
examples.cn: 纱门上有一层细钢丝网。

examples.en: Our plans do not mesh with the weather forecasts.
examples.cn: 我们的计划与天气预报对不上。

examples.en: The old clock stopped because its gears failed to mesh.
examples.cn: 这座旧钟停了，因为齿轮没有咬合上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没（méi）」——网眼那么密，小鱼没处钻；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语或低地德语 maesche（网眼）→ 中古英语 mesh（网眼）→ 现代英语兼指整张网、网格、啮合与契合，核心义「交织成孔」。

sensesIntro.en: Mesh begins with the opening in a net, widens to the whole net, then to interlocking teeth and to things fitting together.
sensesIntro.cn: mesh 从网眼开始，扩大到整张网，再借「互锁」意象指齿轮啮合，并引申为配合一致。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads crossing to leave small even squares.
core.cn: 核心意象：线条交叉，留下均匀的小方格。

branches.en: The woven net is the material sense.
branches.cn: 编织的网是材料义项。

branches.en: One opening is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 单个孔洞是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Gear meshing borrows the crossing and locking image.
branches.cn: 齿轮啮合借用了交叉互锁的意象。

branches.en: The verb of interlocking grows from the noun.
branches.cn: 表示咬合的动词由名词发展而来。

branches.en: Agreement between plans and protective netting both extend the woven picture.
branches.cn: 计划之间的一致与防护网都是编织画面的延伸。

intro.en: Mesh is a native Germanic borrowing with few affixes, its family built on meshes, meshed, and meshwork.
intro.cn: mesh 是日耳曼语来源的短词，词缀很少，词族由 meshes、meshed 与 meshwork 构成。

latinIntro.en: Mesh has no Latin origin, so the same-root Latin entries are naturally empty.
latinIntro.cn: mesh 没有拉丁语来源，因此同源的拉丁词条为空。

items.example: Mesh is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: mesh 是基础名词。

items.example: Mesh is also a verb.
items.exampleCN: mesh 也可以作动词。

items.example: The suffix -es forms meshes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -es 构成 meshes。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms meshed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 meshed。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms meshing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 meshing。

items.example: The suffix -y forms meshy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 meshy。

items.example: The element -work forms meshwork.
items.exampleCN: 构件 -work 构成 meshwork。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unmesh.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unmesh。

items.example: Wire combines with mesh as wire mesh.
items.exampleCN: wire 与 mesh 组合成 wire mesh。

definition_zh: 使着迷；吸引；对……施催眠术
definition_en: to hold the attention of someone completely, as if under a spell, or to put someone into a hypnotic state
core_image: 一双钉住对方的眼睛，让人动弹不得、目不转睛
scene: 厅里的人都停下了脚步，被古老钟表机芯里摆动的金摆锤牢牢吸住了目光。Everyone in the hall stopped and was mesmerized by the golden pendulum swinging inside the old clock.
sceneCN: 这里 mesmerized 是「被迷住、看呆了」（第 1 个义项：使人完全着迷）；句意：厅里的人都停下了脚步，被古老钟表机芯里摆动的金摆锤牢牢吸住了目光。

pos.zh: 使着迷；使入迷；对……施催眠术

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转为形容词，义为「令人着迷的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「入迷的；看呆了的」
由人名 Mesmer 加 -ism 构成，义为「催眠术；昏迷术」
由人名加 -ist 构成，义为「施催眠术者」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「施催眠；着迷状态」

senses.title: To hold someone spellbound
senses.definition: to fascinate someone so completely that they cannot look away
senses.definitionCN: 把人吸引到无法移开视线的程度
senses.example: The children were mesmerized by the puppets.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被木偶戏迷住了。
senses.why: Mesmer was a healer famous for holding patients in a trance, so his name came to mean casting a spell on the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 梅斯梅尔以让病人进入恍惚状态闻名，于是他的姓氏变成了「钉住目光」的动作。

senses.title: To seize the attention of a crowd
senses.definition: of a speech, show, or speaker, to capture the full attention of an audience
senses.definitionCN: 演讲、表演或表演者牢牢抓住观众注意
senses.example: Her voice mesmerizes the whole theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音让整个剧场的人都听痴了。
senses.why: A performer who holds every eye acts like the famous hypnotist, so the spell image moves to performance.
senses.whyCN: 能让所有人目不转睛的表演者，就像那位著名催眠师，咒语般的画面转到了表演上。

senses.title: To put someone into a trance
senses.definition: to induce a hypnotic state in a person
senses.definitionCN: 使某人进入催眠或恍惚状态
senses.example: In the play, the doctor tries to mesmerize his patient.
senses.exampleCN: 剧中医生试图对病人施催眠术。
senses.why: The literal sense is the oldest: following Mesmer, to hypnotize was to mesmerize.
senses.whyCN: 字面义最古老：跟随梅斯梅尔的说法，施加催眠就叫 mesmerize。

senses.title: To freeze someone in place
senses.definition: to make someone unable to move or react because they are so amazed
senses.definitionCN: 因极度惊异而使人不能动、不能反应
senses.example: The dancers stood mesmerized at the edge of the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者们在台边站着看呆了。
senses.why: Trance means stillness, so being mesmerized includes standing still, frozen by what you see.
senses.whyCN: 恍惚状态本身就是静止的，所以被迷住也包括站着不动、被所见定住。

senses.title: To fascinate in a magnetic way
senses.definition: to attract someone so strongly that other things stop mattering
senses.definitionCN: 强烈吸引某人，以至于其他事都不再重要
senses.example: The old city has mesmerized visitors for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古城数百年来一直让来访者着迷。
senses.why: A spell pulls attention like a magnet, so the word also covers a lasting, gentle fascination.
senses.whyCN: 咒语像磁铁一样拉扯注意，于是这个词也涵盖持久而温和的迷恋。

intro.en: Mesmerize is built on the surname of Franz Mesmer, a physician in Vienna and Paris whose animal magnetism was also called mesmerism.
intro.cn: mesmerize 来自奥地利医生梅斯梅尔的姓氏，他的「动物磁力」疗法也被称为催眠术。

items.en: The surname Mesmer is of German origin, with no direct link to Latin.
items.cn: 梅斯梅尔这个姓氏源于德语，与拉丁语没有直接关系。

items.en: Around the seventeen eighties French gave mesmerism for his practice.
items.cn: 十八世纪八九十年代前后，法语以他的姓造出表示其疗法的词。

items.en: English adopted mesmerism, then formed the verb mesmerize.
items.cn: 英语借入催眠术一词，再据此造出动词 mesmerize。

items.en: The verb first meant to hypnotize, then to put into a trance.
items.cn: 这个动词最初表示施催眠，后来表示使人进入恍惚状态。

items.en: Everyday use loosens the meaning to amaze or captivate.
items.cn: 现代日常用法把意思放宽为「令人惊叹、使人着迷」。

note.en: Mesmerize is an eponym, a name turned into a verb, close to trance words and to ordinary words of fascination.
note.cn: mesmerize 是由人名转成的动词，与恍惚一类词以及普通的「迷人」词相邻。

entries.definition: a hypnotic practice named after Mesmer
entries.definitionCN: 由同一人名加 -ism 构成，义为催眠术

entries.definition: a person who hypnotizes others
entries.definitionCN: 由同一人名加 -ist 构成，义为施催眠术者

entries.definition: to learn by heart
entries.definitionCN: 与 mesmerize 拼写相近，但源自 memory，意为「记住」

entries.definition: to attract attention strongly
to hold the interest of someone
to put someone into a trance

normalIntro.en: Mesmerize is a person turned into a verb: Dr Mesmer, the hypnotist, now lives in the word.
normalIntro.cn: mesmerize 是一个人名变成动词：催眠师梅斯梅尔医生如今活在这个词里。

normal.en: The old spelling mesmerise is usual in British text.
normal.cn: 英式文本常用拼写 mesmerise。

normal.en: Be mesmerized by a scene means to be unable to look away.
normal.cn: be mesmerized by 某物，就是无法移开视线。

normal.en: The suffix -ize makes a verb from the surname Mesmer.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ize 把姓氏 Mesmer 变成动词。

normal.en: The adjective mesmerizing describes things that hold attention.
normal.cn: 形容词 mesmerizing 形容牢牢抓住注意的事物。

normal.en: Compare memorise: memory builds memorize, Mesmer builds mesmerize.
normal.cn: 对比 memorize：memory 造出 memorize，Mesmer 造出 mesmerize。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket watch swinging slowly before your eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只怀表在你眼前慢慢摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd turning as one to a bright stage.
abstract.cn: 想象人群齐刷刷转向明亮的舞台。

abstract.en: Picture eyes locked on a slow, quiet pendulum.
abstract.cn: 想象一双眼睛钉在一个缓慢安静的摆锤上。

examples.en: The documentary mesmerized viewers from the first minute.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片从第一分钟起就让观众入了迷。

examples.en: He was mesmerized by the flickering light on the water.
examples.cn: 他被水面上闪动的光看得入了神。

examples.en: The antique merchant would mesmerize customers with stories about each object.
examples.cn: 这位古董商总用每件物品的故事把顾客迷住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「美姿」——一个人姿色太美，旁人全被吸住目光；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 德语姓氏 Mesmer（维也纳医生梅斯梅尔的姓）→ 法语催眠术 → 英语 mesmerism → mesmerize，核心义「以目光施展魔咒」。

sensesIntro.en: Mesmerize starts as the trance of Dr Mesmer, then moves to captivating a crowd, and finally to plain fascination or amazement.
sensesIntro.cn: mesmerize 先从梅斯梅尔的催眠恍惚出发，再指抓住观众，最后泛指着迷与惊叹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes locked on a swinging pendulum.
core.cn: 核心意象：双眼钉在摆动的摆锤上。

branches.en: Being spellbound is the central everyday sense.
branches.cn: 被钉住目光是核心的日常义项。

branches.en: A speaker holding a crowd is the show sense.
branches.cn: 演讲者抓住全场是演出相关义项。

branches.en: Hypnotizing a patient is the literal old sense.
branches.cn: 对病人施催眠是古老的字面义项。

branches.en: Standing frozen comes from the stillness of a trance.
branches.cn: 呆立不动来自恍惚状态的静止。

branches.en: A spell and a lasting attraction both pull attention.
branches.cn: 咒语与持久的吸引力都在拉扯注意力。

intro.en: Mesmerize is an eponym, built by adding -ize to a surname, with a family of mesmerizing, mesmerism, and mesmerist.
intro.cn: mesmerize 来自人名加词尾 -ize，词族包括 mesmerizing、mesmerism 与 mesmerist。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind the surname, and its -ize ending is really Greek, so the Latin entries are empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个姓氏背后没有拉丁词根，-ize 词尾实际源自希腊语，因此拉丁词条为空。

items.example: Mesmer is the name behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: Mesmer 是这个动词背后的姓氏。

items.example: The suffix -ize turns a name into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 把姓氏变成动词。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms mesmerism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 mesmerism。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms mesmerist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 mesmerist。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms mesmerizing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 mesmerizing。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms mesmerized.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 mesmerized。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms mesmerization.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 mesmerization。

items.example: The suffix -ise gives mesmerise.
items.exampleCN: 英式词尾 -ise 构成 mesmerise。

items.example: Enrapture is a near neighbour built with en-.
items.exampleCN: enrapture 是相近词，由前缀 en- 构成。

definition_zh: 准金属；类金属；具有金属与非金属双重性质的化学元素
definition_en: a chemical element that has some properties of metals and some of nonmetals
core_image: 一块灰色发亮的矿石，摸起来像金属，却几乎不导电
scene: 化学课的展台上摆着几小块闪亮的矿石，标签上写着非金属的名字。The teacher called boron a metalloid because it conducts heat but hardly any electricity.
sceneCN: 这里 metalloid 是「准金属」（第 1 个义项：性质介于金属与非金属之间的化学元素）；句意为老师把硼叫作准金属，因为它导热却几乎不导电。

pos.zh: 准金属；类金属；性质似金属的元素

collocations.zh: 类金属性能；准金属表现

derivatives.zh: 由 metalloid 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「准金属的」
由 metalloidal 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以准金属的方式」

senses.title: An element between metal and nonmetal
senses.definition: a chemical element whose properties lie between those of metals and nonmetals
senses.definitionCN: 性质介于金属与非金属之间的化学元素
senses.example: Boron, silicon and arsenic are usually classed as metalloids.
senses.exampleCN: 硼、硅和砷通常被归为准金属。
senses.why: Metal plus the Greek suffix -oid, meaning like, gives a substance that looks like a metal but does not behave like one.
senses.whyCN: 表示「金属」的部分加上希腊语后缀 -oid（像……的），就得到一种外表像金属、行为却不像金属的物质。

senses.title: A lookalike in older chemistry
senses.definition: in older chemical writing, a name given to elements thought to imitate metals
senses.definitionCN: 在早期化学文献中，对被认为模仿金属的元素所给的名称
senses.example: Early chemists used the word for substances that merely resembled metals.
senses.exampleCN: 早期化学家把这个词用在仅仅与金属相似的物质上。
senses.why: Before the modern classification, the suffix -oid carried its full force: the word named anything that imitated a metal in look or behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 在现代分类出现之前，后缀 -oid 保留了完整的「模仿」含义，凡是外观或行为像金属的东西都可以这样称呼。

senses.title: The adjectival sense
senses.definition: having some, but not all, of the properties of a metal
senses.definitionCN: 具有金属的部分性质，但并非全部性质
senses.example: Silicon shows metalloid behaviour at ordinary temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 硅在常温下表现出准金属特性。
senses.why: The same word serves as an adjective because the -oid ending already means like, so the noun turns into a description without any change.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能作形容词，因为 -oid 本身就表示「像……的」，名词无需变形就可以修饰别的名词。

senses.title: A non-metal that shines
senses.definition: a nonmetallic substance with a metallic lustre
senses.definitionCN: 具有金属光泽的非金属物质
senses.example: The mineral has a metalloid appearance but is otherwise a poor conductor.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物外观似金属，但在其他方面导电很差。
senses.why: Ordinary language keeps the visual strand of the suffix: a shiny grey surface reads as metal even when the chemistry says otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言保留了后缀中「看起来像」的那一层：灰亮的表面容易被读成金属，即使化学性质并非如此。

intro.en: Metalloid joins the Greek noun metal, which passed through Latin, with the Greek suffix -oeides, meaning like, in the manner of other scientific coinages.
intro.cn: metalloid 由经拉丁语进入英语的 metal（金属）与希腊语后缀 -oeides（像……的）拼接而成，模仿了当时的科学造词方式。

items.en: Metallon names a mine, a quarry, or the ore taken from it.
items.cn: metallon 指矿坑、采石场，或从中取出的矿石。

items.en: Metallum keeps the mining sense of ore and metal.
items.cn: metallum 保留「矿石、金属」的采矿含义。

items.en: Metal settles into English meaning a solid shiny element.
items.cn: metal 在英语中稳定下来，指有光泽的固态元素。

items.en: The element -oeides means having the form of, a sense already used in words like spheroid.
items.cn: 构词成分 -oeides 意为「具有……形状」，在 spheroid 一类词中已是这种用法。

items.en: Chemists build metal and -oid into a label for metal-like substances.
items.cn: 化学家把 metal 与 -oid 组合成称呼似金属物质的标签。

items.en: Modern chemistry narrows the word to elements on the borderline.
items.cn: 现代化学把这个词收窄到处于分界线上的元素。

note.en: Metalloid sits in the metal word family; its spelling is close to metal and metallurgy, and its meaning borders on semiconductor and nonmetal.
note.cn: metalloid 属于 metal 这一词族，拼写与 metal、metallurgy 接近，意思上与 semiconductor 和 nonmetal 相邻。

entries.definition: a solid material with a shiny surface that conducts heat and electricity
entries.definitionCN: 有光泽、能导热导电的固态材料

entries.definition: made of metal or looking like metal
the science of extracting and working metals
a material that conducts electricity only under certain conditions
entries.definitionCN: 在一定条件下才导电的材料；半导体

entries.definition: a chemical element that lacks the properties of a metal
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏金属性质的化学元素；非金属

entries.definition: a pure substance made of one kind of atom
entries.definitionCN: 由同一种原子构成的纯净物；元素

normalIntro.en: Metalloid is metal plus the ending -oid, which means like; it is a metal lookalike that stops short of being one.
normalIntro.cn: metalloid 是 metal 加上表示「像……」的结尾 -oid，也就是一个像金属、却算不上金属的东西。

normal.en: The -oid ending means like, as in humanoid and asteroid.
normal.cn: 结尾 -oid 表示「像……的」，如 humanoid 与 asteroid。

normal.en: A metalloid looks metallic but conducts electricity poorly.
normal.cn: 准金属看起来像金属，导电性却很差。

normal.en: Metal plus -oid spells metalloid and keeps the double l.
normal.cn: metal 加 -oid 拼成 metalloid，保留双写字母 l。

normal.en: Silicon and germanium are the most familiar metalloids.
normal.cn: 硅和锗是最常见、最熟悉的准金属。

normal.en: Compare nonmetal: a metalloid is on the middle ground, a nonmetal is at the far end.
normal.cn: 对比 nonmetal：准金属处于中间地带，非金属则在另一端。

abstract.en: Picture a grey lamp post that turns out to be made of plastic.
abstract.cn: 想象一根灰亮的灯柱，后来才发现是塑料做的。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge built halfway across a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只修到河中央的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a coin that shines on one side and rusts on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，一面闪亮，另一面却在生锈。

examples.en: The periodic table places the metalloids along a staircase line.
examples.cn: 元素周期表把准金属排在一条阶梯状分界线上。

examples.en: Germanium behaves like a metalloid in most laboratory tests.
examples.cn: 在多数实验室测试中，锗表现得像一种准金属。

examples.en: Teachers often ask students to sort the elements into metals, metalloids and nonmetals.
examples.cn: 老师常让学生把元素分成金属、准金属和非金属三类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖它楼的」——卖金属的楼里混进一块假货，像金属却不是金属；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 希腊语 metallon「矿、矿石」→ 拉丁语 metallum「矿石、金属」→ 英语 metal「金属」；希腊语后缀 -oeides「像……的」经拉丁化成为英语 -oid。两者合成 metalloid，字面义为「像金属的东西」，核心义是「介于金属与非金属之间的元素」。

sensesIntro.en: Metalloid starts as a chemical label for borderline elements, echoes an older use for metal lookalikes, and then moves into adjectival and everyday description.
sensesIntro.cn: metalloid 先指处于分界线上的化学元素，再回响早期对似金属物质的称呼，随后扩展为形容词用法与日常描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey ore that shines like metal but barely carries a current.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块灰亮的矿石，像金属一样反光，却几乎不导电。

branches.en: The element between metal and nonmetal is the modern chemical sense.
branches.cn: 介于金属与非金属之间的元素，是现代化学义。

branches.en: Older chemistry takes the word literally, for a metal lookalike.
branches.cn: 早期化学按字面理解，指似金属的物质。

branches.en: The adjective use drops the noun and describes the property.
branches.cn: 形容词用法省去名词，直接描述这种性质。

branches.en: Both a metalloid element and a nonmetal with metallic lustre share the shine.
branches.cn: 准金属元素与有金属光泽的非金属，都共享「发亮」这一外观。

branches.en: The older noun and the adjective both rest on the same like suffix.
branches.cn: 较早的名词用法与形容词用法，都建立在同一个表示「像」的后缀上。

intro.en: Metalloid is a compound of the metal root and a Greek shape suffix, so the family runs from metal to metallurgy to metalloid.
intro.cn: metalloid 由表示金属的词根与希腊语的形状后缀组合而成，所以词族从 metal 延伸到 metallurgy 再到 metalloid。

latinIntro.en: Latin metallum supplies the metal root, and the Greek suffix -oeides reaches English as -oid by way of Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metallum 提供金属词根，希腊语后缀 -oeides 则借拉丁语词形进入英语，成为 -oid。

items.example: Metal gives the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: metal 提供这个词的前半部分。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms words such as humanoid and asteroid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成 humanoid、asteroid 等词。

items.example: Greek -oeides is the deeper source of -oid.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 -oeides 是 -oid 的更早来源。

items.example: Metalloid names the middle group of the table.
items.exampleCN: metalloid 指周期表中的中间一族。

items.example: Metalloidal adds the adjective suffix -al.
items.exampleCN: metalloidal 加上形容词后缀 -al。

items.example: Metallic shares the metal root with -ic.
items.exampleCN: metallic 以 -ic 共享金属词根。

items.example: Metallurgy joins metal with the Greek word for work.
items.exampleCN: metallurgy 把金属与希腊语「劳作」组合起来。

items.example: Metalliferous joins metal with the Latin word for carrying.
items.exampleCN: metalliferous 把金属与拉丁语「携带」组合起来。

items.example: Nonmetal adds the negative prefix non- to metal.
items.exampleCN: nonmetal 在 metal 前加否定前缀 non-。

definition_zh: 隐喻；暗喻；比喻；能承载比喻意义的象征
definition_en: a way of describing something by calling it another thing that shares a key quality with it
core_image: 一个人把一件东西举到另一件东西旁边，让你看见它们相似
scene: 诗人写时间是个小偷，读者觉得写得很妙。Critics praised the metaphor because it made an abstract idea feel concrete.
sceneCN: 这里 metaphor 是「隐喻、暗喻」（第 1 个义项：借另一事物来描写某事的修辞方式）；句意为评论家称赞这个隐喻，因为它让抽象的观念变得具体可感。

collocations.zh: 混杂比喻；前后不一致的比喻
延伸隐喻；贯穿全篇的比喻
陈旧的隐喻；已失去新鲜感的比喻

derivatives.zh: 由 metaphor 加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「隐喻的、比喻的」
由 metaphorical 加 -ly 构成，义为「以隐喻的方式、比喻地」
与 metaphorical 同义，古代修辞学色彩更浓，义为「隐喻性的」
由 metaphor 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「用隐喻表达」

senses.title: A figure of speech built on likeness
senses.definition: a figure of speech in which one thing is described as if it were another
senses.definitionCN: 把一事物当作另一事物来描写的修辞方式
senses.example: Calling the city a jungle is a familiar metaphor.
senses.exampleCN: 把城市叫作丛林，是大家熟知的隐喻。
senses.why: The Greek word meta means across and pherein means to carry, so a metaphor carries a name across from one thing to another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 meta 意为「越过」，pherein 意为「运送」，隐喻就是把一个名字从一物运送到另一物上。

senses.title: A concrete image for an idea
senses.titleCN: （承载抽象概念的）比喻性形象
senses.definition: an image or story that represents a larger abstract idea
senses.definitionCN: 代表更大抽象思想的形象或故事
senses.example: In the novel, the house stands as a metaphor for memory.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中，那座房子是记忆的隐喻。
senses.why: Because the carried name brings a visible thing, a concrete image can stand in for an invisible idea.
senses.whyCN: 被运送过来的名字带来可见的形象，因此具体形象可以代替看不见的思想。

senses.title: A way of framing experience
senses.definition: a way of speaking that shapes how people think about a topic
senses.definitionCN: 一种说法，会影响人们如何看待某个话题
senses.example: Treating time as money is a metaphor we live by without noticing.
senses.exampleCN: 把时间当作金钱，是我们不加察觉地依循的一种隐喻。
senses.why: Repeated metaphors do not just decorate thought; the transferred frame slowly becomes the way the topic is understood.
senses.whyCN: 反复使用的隐喻不只是修饰想法，被搬运过来的框架会慢慢变成理解这个话题的默认方式。

senses.title: An archaic transfer
senses.definition: an antiquated sense of carrying a word or a property from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 过时的义项：把词语或性质从一处转移到另一处
senses.example: Old grammars used the word for a transferred name.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的语法书用这个词指称名字的转移。
senses.why: The literal sense of carrying across was once alive here and survives inside borrowings such as metabolism.
senses.whyCN: 「搬运过去」的字面意义曾在此词中鲜活，并在 metabolism 等借词里留下痕迹。

intro.en: Metaphor descends from Greek metapherein, literally to carry across, and first entered English through works on rhetoric.
intro.cn: metaphor 源自希腊语 metapherein，字面义为「运过去」，最初经修辞学著作进入英语。

items.en: Meta means across or beyond.
items.cn: meta 意为「越过、超越」。

items.en: Pherein means to carry or bring.
items.cn: pherein 意为「运送、带来」。

items.en: Metaphora names a transfer of meaning in speech.
items.cn: metaphora 指言语中意义的转移。

items.en: Rhetorical teaching passes the word on as Latin metaphora.
items.cn: 修辞教学经由拉丁语 metaphora 传递这个词。

items.en: Metaphor enters English with the revival of classical rhetoric.
items.cn: 随着古典修辞学复兴，metaphor 进入英语。

items.en: Linguistics widens it to everyday thought and language.
items.cn: 语言学把它扩展到日常思维与日常语言。

note.en: Metaphor belongs to the meta- carrying family, and among figures of speech it borders on simile and analogy.
note.cn: metaphor 属于以 meta- 开头、含有「运送」义的词族，在修辞格中与 simile 和 analogy 相邻。

entries.definition: used as a metaphor
in a figurative way
a complete change of form
a comparison using like or as
an explanation that shows how two things are similar
entries.definitionCN: 类比；用相似之处作解释

entries.definition: a picture made in words for the reader
entries.definitionCN: 意象；为读者营造的画面

normalIntro.en: Metaphor is built from meta across and the carrying root pher-, which together picture a word carried onto another thing.
normalIntro.cn: metaphor 由表示「越过」的 meta 与表示「运送」的词根 pher- 构成，合起来就是一个词被运送到另一物上的画面。

normal.en: Meta and pher spell the carrying part of the word.
normal.cn: meta 与 pher 拼出了这个词里「运送」的那部分。

normal.en: A metaphor says one thing is another, a simile uses like or as.
normal.cn: 隐喻直接说甲是乙，明喻则用 like 或 as。

normal.en: A mixed metaphor joins two clashing images and sounds clumsy.
normal.cn: 混杂比喻把两个冲突的形象拼在一起，听起来很别扭。

normal.en: An extended metaphor stretches one image across a whole poem.
normal.cn: 延伸隐喻把同一个形象铺展到整首诗里。

normal.en: The family is regular: metaphorical, metaphorically, metaphorize.
normal.cn: 这个词族很规整：metaphorical、metaphorically、metaphorize。

abstract.en: Picture two objects held side by side until you see the shared shape.
abstract.cn: 想象把两件东西并排放置，直到你看清它们共有的形状。

abstract.en: Imagine a label carried across a room and stuck onto a new object.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签被搬到房间另一头，贴到一件新东西上。

abstract.en: Think of a thin screen dropped over a city so that it looks like a forest.
abstract.cn: 想象给城市罩上一层薄纱，看上去就像一片森林。

examples.en: The writer uses the sea as a metaphor for freedom.
examples.cn: 作者把大海用作自由的隐喻。

examples.en: His speech was full of metaphors about journeys and maps.
examples.cn: 他的演讲充满了关于旅程与地图的隐喻。

examples.en: A mixed metaphor can ruin an otherwise strong argument.
examples.cn: 一个混杂比喻可能毁掉一段本来有力的论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没它法儿」——说不清的事，只好借别的东西来说；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关，真正的词源是「搬运」。

root: 希腊语 meta「越过、超越」+ pherein「运送」→ metaphora「意义转移」→ 拉丁语 metaphora → 英语 metaphor。同源词包括 periphery（外围），核心义是「把名字从一物搬运到另一物」。

sensesIntro.en: Metaphor starts as the rhetorical act of carrying a name across, then the concrete image that does the carrying, then the frame it builds, and at last a now archaic word for the transfer itself.
sensesIntro.cn: metaphor 先指把名字搬运过去的修辞动作，再指承担这种搬运的具体形象，接着指它建构的理解框架，最后剩下一个已废弃的、表示「转移」本身的义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name carried across and set down on another thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被搬到另一件东西上。

branches.en: Carrying a name across yields the rhetorical figure.
branches.cn: 把名字搬运过去，就产生了修辞格本身。

branches.en: The transferred name brings a visible image into an abstract argument.
branches.cn: 被搬运的名字把可见形象带入抽象议论。

branches.en: A metaphor used again and again becomes a frame for thinking.
branches.cn: 反复使用的隐喻会成为思考的框架。

branches.en: The oldest sense keeps the plain act of carrying across.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项保留了「搬运过去」这一朴素动作。

branches.en: The figure and the image are one act seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 修辞格与形象是同一个动作的两面。

intro.en: Metaphor rests on the Greek prefix meta- and the carrying root pher-, and English builds its whole adjective and adverb family on top of it.
intro.cn: metaphor 建立在希腊语前缀 meta- 与表示「运送」的词根 pher- 之上，英语再在它上面发展出整套形容词与副词词族。

latinIntro.en: The Greek verb pherein, to carry, reaches Latin through words such as phosphorus, and Latin metaphora passes the noun on to English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语动词 pherein（运送）通过 phosphorus 等词进入拉丁语，拉丁语名词 metaphora 又把这个词交给英语。

items.example: The prefix meta- appears in metaphor and metamorphosis.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 meta- 出现在 metaphor 与 metamorphosis 中。

items.example: The root pher- also appears in periphery.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pher- 也出现在 periphery 中。

items.example: The suffix -phor appears in metaphor and semaphore.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -phor 出现在 metaphor 与 semaphore 中。

items.example: Metaphor keeps the carrying image.
items.exampleCN: metaphor 保留了「搬运」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms metaphorical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ical 构成 metaphorical。

items.example: Metaphorical describes figurative language.
items.exampleCN: metaphorical 描述比喻性的语言。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms metaphorically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 metaphorically。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms metaphorize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 metaphorize。

items.meaning: the outer edge of an area
items.example: Periphery carries the same Greek root with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: periphery 用不同前缀共享同一希腊词根。

definition_zh: 隐喻的；比喻的；比喻意义上的；非字面的
definition_en: used or understood as a metaphor rather than in the literal sense
core_image: 一句话被举起来，挪到另一件事上，字面意思随之被放下
scene: 朋友抱怨说自己的日程表是一座要塌的桥，我不确定该当真还是只当个比方。I could not tell whether the remark was literal or metaphorical, so I simply nodded.
sceneCN: 这里 metaphorical 是「比喻的、非字面的」（第 1 个义项：按隐喻而非字面来理解）；句意为分不清这句话是字面意思还是比喻说法，只好点头。

pos.zh: 隐喻的；比喻的；非字面的

collocations.zh: 隐喻性语言；比喻性语言

collocations.phrase: a metaphorical slap on the wrist

derivatives.zh: 由 metaphorical 加 -ly 构成，义为「比喻地、以隐喻方式」
metaphorical 的基础名词，义为「隐喻、暗喻」
与 metaphorical 同义，由 metaphor 直接加 -ic 构成，义为「隐喻性的」
由 metaphoric 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「隐喻性」

senses.title: Used as a figure of speech
senses.definition: expressing one thing in terms of another, not in its literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 借另一事物来表达，而非按字面意义
senses.example: Do not take his remark literally; it was metaphorical.
senses.exampleCN: 别按字面理解他的话，那只是比喻的说法。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ical to metaphor, so it describes anything that works by carrying a name across from another thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 metaphor 后加 -ical，所以凡是靠「把名字搬运过去」来起作用的东西，都可以这样描述。

senses.title: Understood in a loose sense
senses.titleCN: 比喻意义上的；打个比方的
senses.definition: used loosely to mean something like, but not exactly
senses.definitionCN: 宽松地说，表示大致如此但并非确切如此
senses.example: A metaphorical mountain of paperwork landed on her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 一座比喻意义上的文件大山压到了她的桌上。
senses.why: When a concrete noun is stretched onto an abstract quantity, the borrowing sense turns into a hedge word meaning more or less.
senses.whyCN: 当具体名词被挪用到抽象数量上时，「借用」之义就变成了表示「大致如此」的委婉词。

senses.title: Of literary or figurative style
senses.definition: full of or given to figurative language
senses.definitionCN: 充满比喻或倾向于使用比喻语言的
senses.example: Her metaphorical style suits poetry better than contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 她富于比喻的文风更适合写诗，而非起草合同。
senses.why: From describing a single phrase the adjective extends to a whole manner of writing, described by how much it borrows names.
senses.whyCN: 从描述一个说法扩展到整种文风，评价标准就是它借用了多少外来的名字。

intro.en: Metaphorical is formed inside English from the Greek noun metaphor and the English suffix -ical, and it keeps the older -ic bypass form beside it.
intro.cn: metaphorical 是在英语内部由希腊语名词 metaphor 与英语后缀 -ical 构成的，旁边还保留了更早的 -ic 形式 metaphoric。

items.en: Meta means across and pherein means to carry.
items.cn: meta 意为「越过」，pherein 意为「运送」。

items.en: Metaphora names a transferred meaning in rhetoric.
items.cn: 修辞学中 metaphora 指意义的转移。

items.en: The noun metaphor enters English with classical rhetoric.
items.cn: 名词 metaphor 随古典修辞学进入英语。

items.en: The adjective metaphoric comes first from -ic.
items.cn: 形容词先以 -ic 的形式 metaphoric 出现。

items.en: The -ical form spread and became the everyday adjective.
items.cn: -ical 的形式逐渐普及，成为日常使用的形容词。

note.en: Metaphorical is the adjective of metaphor; in spelling it brushes against metal and metamorphic, and in meaning it borders on figurative and symbolic.
note.cn: metaphorical 是 metaphor 的形容词形式；拼写上与 metal、metamorphic 容易混，意思上与 figurative、symbolic 相邻。

entries.definition: a figure of speech that carries a name across
in a figurative way
changed in form, as rock under pressure
entries.definitionCN: 变质性的（岩石在压力下变形）；只是前缀相近，词尾来源不同

entries.definition: not literal, using images for effect
standing for a larger idea
taking words in their usual sense

normalIntro.en: Metaphorical wears the -ical coat of its noun metaphor, so it always points back to the carrying image.
normalIntro.cn: metaphorical 披着名词 metaphor 的 -ical 外衣，因此总是指回那个「搬运」的意象。

normal.en: The ending -ical makes adjectives: metaphor becomes metaphorical.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ical 构成形容词：metaphor 变成 metaphorical。

normal.en: In a metaphorical sense means as a figure of speech.
normal.cn: in a metaphorical sense 意为在比喻意义上。

normal.en: The adverb metaphorically drops -al and adds -ly.
normal.cn: 副词 metaphorically 去掉 -al 再加上 -ly。

normal.en: Metaphorical sits opposite literal in most pairs of sentences.
normal.cn: 在多数句子里，metaphorical 与 literal 相对。

normal.en: Keep metaphoric for older style and metaphorical for everyday use.
normal.cn: metaphoric 偏旧式文风，metaphorical 用于日常表达。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that only exists in the sentence, not on any map.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只存在于句子里的桥，地图上根本找不到。

abstract.en: Imagine a word taking off its literal coat and wearing a borrowed one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词脱下字面的外套，换上借来的那件。

abstract.en: Think of a red arrow on a diagram that means risk, not colour.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的红色箭头表示危险，而不是指颜色。

examples.en: The phrase storm of criticism is metaphorical rather than literal.
examples.cn: 「批评的风暴」这一说法是比喻性的，并非字面意义。

examples.en: She spoke metaphorically when she said the project was on fire.
examples.cn: 她说项目着火时，只是打了个比方。

examples.en: Teachers often ask pupils to separate metaphorical language from plain description.
examples.cn: 老师常要求学生把比喻性语言与平实描述区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没它法儿」再加个ical——说不清的时候，只好借个比方来说；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 meta「越过」+ pherein「运送」→ metaphora → 英语 metaphor；英语在名词后加后缀 -ical 构成形容词 metaphorical，核心义仍是「借别的事物来说，而非按字面」。

sensesIntro.en: Metaphorical begins as the plain adjective of metaphor, loosens into a hedge meaning so to speak, and finally describes a whole figurative style.
sensesIntro.cn: metaphorical 先是 metaphor 的普通形容词，随后松动为表示「打个比方」的委婉说法，最后用来描述整种比喻性文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence lifted from its literal place and set down elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话从字面位置被举起，放到别处。

branches.en: The plain adjective of metaphor is the core sense.
branches.cn: metaphor 的普通形容词用法是核心义项。

branches.en: The hedge sense means roughly or as it were.
branches.cn: 委婉义项表示「大致如此」「可以说是」。

branches.en: A whole style is judged by how much it borrows names.
branches.cn: 整种文风按它借用了多少名字来评判。

branches.en: Both senses rely on the same jump away from the literal.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖同一个「离开字面」的跳跃。

branches.en: A single metaphorical phrase and a metaphorical style differ only in scale.
branches.cn: 单个比喻说法与比喻性文风，区别只在规模。

intro.en: Metaphorical is a two layer build: the Greek meta- and pher- form the noun, and the English -ical and -ly extend it.
intro.cn: metaphorical 是两层构造：希腊语 meta- 与 pher- 构成名词，英语的 -ical 与 -ly 再把它扩展成形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin metaphora carries the Greek noun into English, and the English suffixes -ic and -ical shape both adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metaphora 把希腊语名词带入英语，英语后缀 -ic 与 -ical 则塑造出两个形容词形式。

items.example: The prefix meta- opens metaphor and metamorphosis.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 meta- 是 metaphor 与 metamorphosis 的开头。

items.example: The root pher- also appears in periphery.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pher- 也出现在 periphery 中。

items.example: Metaphor is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: metaphor 是这个形容词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms metaphoric.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 metaphoric。

items.meaning: relating to, often the everyday form
items.meaningCN: 与……相关的（常为日常形式）
items.example: The suffix -ical forms metaphorical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ical 构成 metaphorical。

items.example: Metaphorical is the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: metaphorical 是日常使用的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms metaphorically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 metaphorically。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms metaphoricity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 metaphoricity。

items.example: Literal is the usual opposite of metaphorical.
items.exampleCN: literal 是 metaphorical 常见的对立词。

definition_zh: 流星；陨星（坠落地球的流星体）
definition_en: a small piece of rock or ice from space that burns brightly as it falls through the layer of air around the Earth, or the bright streak of light it makes
core_image: 夜空里一道划过的亮光，后面拖着一条发光的长尾
scene: 夏夜的草地上，孩子们躺着仰望天空，一道亮光忽然从头顶划过。Last night a meteor flashed across the sky above the village.
sceneCN: 这里 meteor 是「流星」（第 1 个义项：太空碎屑在大气层中燃烧，在夜空划出亮痕）；这道光只是太空小碎块烧起来的痕迹，不是恒星，句意：昨晚一颗流星划过村庄上空的天空。

derivatives.zh: 由 meteor 加表示陨石的词尾构成，指落到地面的陨石
太空中的流星体，由 meteor 加仿星体名构出的词尾构成
由 meteor 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为陨星的，引申为迅速崛起的

senses.title: A streak of light in the sky
senses.definition: the bright streak of light made when a piece of space rock or ice burns up in the air
senses.definitionCN: 太空岩块或冰粒在大气中燃烧时形成的明亮光痕
senses.example: A meteor streaked across the sky just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过，一颗流星划过天空。
senses.why: The Greek root means raised up in the air, which is exactly where the light appears.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根意为「高悬在空中」，而流星正是出现在高空的亮光，所以这个词先把画面放在天空里。

senses.title: The matter that falls
senses.definition: the actual rocky or icy body from space that produces this light
senses.definitionCN: 在太空中运行、产生这种亮光的岩石或冰质天体
senses.example: The museum displays a large meteor found in a desert.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了一块在沙漠中发现的大陨星。
senses.why: The same word shifts from the light to the thing that makes the light, a common shift from effect to cause.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从「光」滑向「发光的东西」，这是由结果指代成因的常见转义。

senses.title: A meteor in family names
senses.definition: used in names and images for something that flashes past quickly and brightly
senses.definitionCN: 用于命名或比喻某种明亮而短暂掠过的事物
senses.example: The band rose like a meteor and vanished within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队如流星般崛起，两年内便消失了。
senses.why: A streak of light is brief and brilliant, so the word easily becomes a picture of sudden fame.
senses.whyCN: 流星明亮而短暂，于是这个词自然成为「一夜成名又迅速消逝」的画面。

intro.en: Meteor goes back through Latin to Greek ta meteora, things high up in the air.
intro.cn: meteor 经由拉丁语上溯到希腊语 ta meteora，意为「高悬空中的事物」。

items.en: Ta meteora means things raised up in the air.
items.cn: ta meteora 意为「被抬到空中的事物」。

items.en: Meteorum names anything appearing in the sky.
items.cn: meteorum 用来称呼一切天象。

items.en: Le meteorre carries the word into French.
items.cn: meteorre 把该词带入法语。

items.en: Meteor first names any atmospheric sight.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 meteor 泛指大气中的一切现象。

items.en: Meteor narrows to the streak of light.
items.cn: 十八世纪 meteor 收窄为划过天空的光痕。

note.en: Meteor shares a sky vocabulary with meteorite and meteoroid, and sits beside other words for falling stars.
note.cn: meteor 与 meteorite、meteoroid 构成一套「天空」词汇，并与其它表示「流星」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a piece of rock from space that has landed on Earth
a small body travelling in space
entries.definitionCN: 在太空中运行的流星体

entries.definition: relating to meteors, or very rapid
the popular name for a meteor seen at night
an exceptionally bright meteor
an icy body that leaves a dusty tail near the Sun
entries.definitionCN: 彗星：靠近太阳时拖出尘埃长尾的冰质天体

normalIntro.en: Meteor is a word for things high up in the air, so it always pictures a light in the sky.
normalIntro.cn: meteor 本是「高悬空中的事物」，所以它总带着天空里一道光的画面。

normal.en: A meteor shower comes when many streaks of light appear in one night.
normal.cn: meteor shower 指一夜之间出现许多光痕的流星雨。

normal.en: Add -ite and you get meteorite, the stone that reaches the ground.
normal.cn: 加上词尾 -ite 得到 meteorite，指落到地面的石头。

normal.en: Add -oid and you get meteoroid, the body still out in space.
normal.cn: 加上词尾 -oid 得到 meteoroid，指仍在太空中的流星体。

normal.en: Meteoric fame is like a meteor, quick to flame and quick to fade.
normal.cn: meteoric 形容的成名就像流星，亮得快也熄得快。

normal.en: Compare comet: a comet travels slowly for weeks, a meteor flashes in a second.
normal.cn: 对比 comet：彗星要缓缓旅行数周，流星只在一瞬间闪亮。

abstract.en: Picture a single bright line drawn quickly across a black sky.
abstract.cn: 想象黑色的天幕上被迅速划出一道亮线。

abstract.en: Imagine a pebble striking the air so fast that it catches fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石子撞进空气，快到燃了起来。

abstract.en: Think of a career that blazes for one season and is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一份事业只辉煌一季便消失无踪。

examples.en: Hundreds of people gathered on the hill to watch the meteor shower.
examples.cn: 数百人聚集在山上观看流星雨。

examples.en: Scientists track each meteoroid before it becomes a bright meteor.
examples.cn: 科学家会追踪每一颗流星体，直到它变成明亮的流星。

examples.en: The meteorite that landed in the field had left a small crater.
examples.cn: 落在田里的陨石留下了一个小坑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米提尔」——想象一颗小米粒被提上高空，撞进大气层后燃成一道亮痕；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古希腊语 μετέωρος（meteōros，高悬空中的）→ ta meteora（空中之物；天象）→ 晚期拉丁语 meteorum → 古法语 → 英语 meteor，核心义「空中掠过的亮物」。

sensesIntro.en: Meteor first names the light in the sky, then the body that makes the light, and finally a figure for brief brilliance.
sensesIntro.cn: meteor 先指天空中的光痕，再指造成光痕的天体，最后成为「短暂辉煌」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright line drawn swiftly across the night sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜空里被迅速划出的一道亮线。

branches.en: The visible streak is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的光痕是日常义项。

branches.en: The falling body is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 坠落的天体是其物质义项。

branches.en: Sudden fame borrows the meteor picture.
branches.cn: 一夜成名借用了流星的画面。

branches.en: The light and the rock are cause and effect.
branches.cn: 光痕与岩块是因果关系。

branches.en: Both feel brilliant and momentary.
branches.cn: 两者都给人明亮而短暂的感觉。

intro.en: Meteor belongs to the Greek family met- and bears the -or noun ending; English adds meteorite, meteoroid and meteoric.
intro.cn: meteor 属于希腊语 met- 词族并带有 -or 名词词尾；英语由此构成 meteorite、meteoroid 与 meteoric。

latinIntro.en: Greek meteōros means raised up, and the derived ta meteora means things high in the air.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 meteōros 意为被抬起、高悬，派生的 ta meteora 意为高空之物。

items.meaning: raised up, high in the air
items.example: Meteoros gives the image of air and height.
items.exampleCN: meteoros 提供「高空」的意象。

items.example: The Greek noun covers all sky sights.
items.exampleCN: 该希腊语名词涵盖一切天象。

items.example: Latin keeps the Greek sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了希腊语含义。

items.example: The ending -or shapes meteor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 meteor。

items.meaningCN: 表示矿物或石块的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ite forms meteorite.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ite 构成 meteorite。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms meteoroid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成 meteoroid。

items.meaningCN: 表示「与……有关」的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ic forms meteoric.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 meteoric。

items.example: Meteorology shares the high sky idea.
items.exampleCN: meteorology 共享「高空天象」的含义。

items.example: The form -logy adds study to meteor.
items.exampleCN: 组合词 -logy 给 meteor 加上「研究」之意。

definition_zh: 微生物；细菌
definition_en: a very small living thing that can only be seen with a microscope, especially one that causes disease
core_image: 一滴水滴在显微镜下显出许多晃动的小黑点
scene: 实验室里，学生把一滴池水滴在玻璃片上，调好焦距，看见许多慢慢蠕动的小点。The pond water is full of tiny microbes, some of which can make people ill.
sceneCN: 这里 microbe 是「微生物」（第 1 个义项：小到必须用显微镜才看得见的活物）；句意：池水里满是微小的微生物，其中一些会让人生病。

derivatives.zh: 由 microbe 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为微生物的
microbe 去尾加 -logy 组合形式构成，义为微生物学
microbe 加 -cide（杀灭）构成，义为杀微生物剂

senses.title: A very small living thing
senses.definition: a living thing so small that it can be seen only with a microscope
senses.definitionCN: 小到只能用显微镜才看得见的活体
senses.example: Some microbes live happily in boiling hot springs.
senses.exampleCN: 有些微生物能自在地生活在滚烫的温泉里。
senses.why: Micro- means small and bios means life, so the word is literally a tiny life form.
senses.whyCN: micro- 表示「微小」，bios 表示「生命」，所以这个词字面上就是「微小的生命」。

senses.title: A germ that causes disease
senses.definition: a harmful microbe that causes infection in people, animals or plants
senses.definitionCN: 在人或动植物身上引起感染的致病微生物
senses.example: Washing your hands removes most disease-causing microbes.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手能去除大多数致病的微生物。
senses.why: Because many familiar microbes bring illness, everyday speech narrows the word to germs.
senses.whyCN: 由于人们熟悉的微生物常带来疾病，日常说法就把这个词收窄为「病菌」。

senses.title: A working partner in a body or field
senses.titleCN: 体内或田间的微生物群落
senses.definition: a population of microbes that lives with us or in the soil and helps us
senses.definitionCN: 与人类共处或生活在土壤中、对我们有帮助的微生物群体
senses.example: Healthy gut microbes help us digest food.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的肠道微生物帮助我们消化食物。
senses.why: Science has reframed the microbe from enemy into partner, so the word now leans on the helpful side.
senses.whyCN: 科学已把这些小生命从敌人改写为伙伴，所以这个词如今更多偏向「有益」的一面。

intro.en: Microbe was built in French in the nineteenth century from Greek mikro-, small, and bios, life.
intro.cn: microbe 于十九世纪在法语中由希腊语 mikro-（微小）与 bios（生命）拼成。

items.en: Mikros means small and bios means life.
items.cn: mikros 意为微小，bios 意为生命。

items.en: Microbe names the tiny life seen under a lens.
items.cn: 十九世纪七十年代法语 microbe 指镜头下的微小活物。

items.en: English borrows microbe from French science.
items.cn: 英语从法国科学界借入 microbe。

items.en: Popular use narrows microbe to germs.
items.cn: 十九世纪九十年代大众用法把 microbe 收窄为病菌。

items.en: Microbial science returns the word to neutral ground.
items.cn: 微生物科学让这个词重新回到中性的立场。

note.en: Microbe belongs to a small family of micro- words and sits beside other names for living things too small to see.
note.cn: microbe 属于以 micro- 开头的一小群词，并与其它「小到看不见的活物」名称相邻。

entries.definition: relating to microbes
the study of microbes
an instrument for viewing very small things
a microbe that can cause disease
a single-celled microbe of one major group
entries.definitionCN: 细菌：一大类单细胞微生物

entries.definition: any agent that causes disease

normalIntro.en: Microbe is a word built from two Greek blocks: small plus life.
normalIntro.cn: microbe 由两个希腊语构件拼成：微小 + 生命。

normal.en: Micro- means small, as in microscope and microwave.
normal.cn: 前缀 micro- 表示微小，如 microscope 与 microwave 中的用法。

normal.en: Bi- in biology and bios means life.
normal.cn: biology 里的 bi-、以及 bios 都表示生命。

normal.en: Microbe plus -ial gives microbial, the adjective for all things microbial.
normal.cn: microbe 加上 -ial 得到 microbial，是所有微生物事物的形容词。

normal.en: Microbe plus -logy gives microbiology, the science of the invisible.
normal.cn: microbe 加上 -logy 得到 microbiology，即研究不可见生命的学问。

normal.en: Compare germ: germ is the everyday word, microbe is the neutral scientific one.
normal.cn: 对比 germ：germ 是日常说法，microbe 是中性而科学的用词。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of pond water as a whole busy city.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴池水本身就是一座热闹的城市。

abstract.en: Imagine tiny dots wriggling under a bright lens.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的镜片下有无数小点在扭动。

abstract.en: Think of a yogurt pot full of helpful workers.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒酸奶里全是勤快的小帮手。

examples.en: Microbes in the soil break down dead leaves and return nutrients.
examples.cn: 土壤中的微生物分解落叶，把养分归还大地。

examples.en: Doctors searched for the microbe that caused the outbreak.
examples.cn: 医生们在寻找引起这次疫情的微生物。

examples.en: Children are taught that some tiny microbes are friendly, not harmful.
examples.cn: 孩子们被教导说，有些微小的微生物是友好的，而不是有害的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈克罗布」——显微镜下盖着一块「布」，布上全是蠕动的小点；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）+ bios（生命）→ 法语 microbe（十九世纪新造）→ 英语 microbe，核心义「微小到看不见的生命」。

sensesIntro.en: Microbe starts as the neutral name for invisible life, then narrows to disease germs, and now widens again toward helpful partners.
sensesIntro.cn: microbe 最初是「看不见的生命」的中性名称，随后收窄为病菌，如今又向「有益伙伴」重新扩开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water alive with tiny moving specks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴水里满是蠕动的小点。

branches.en: The neutral scientific sense names tiny life.
branches.cn: 中性的科学义项指微小的生命。

branches.en: The germ sense focuses on sickness.
branches.cn: 病菌义项聚焦于疾病。

branches.en: The helper sense sees microbes as partners.
branches.cn: 帮手义项把这些小生命看作伙伴。

branches.en: Both describe ordinary microbes doing their work.
branches.cn: 两者都描述在日常生活里干活的微生物。

branches.en: Harmful and helpful microbes share one name.
branches.cn: 有害与有益的微生物共用一个名字。

intro.en: Microbe is built from the Greek elements micro- and bio-, and English extends it with microbial, microbiology and microbicide.
intro.cn: microbe 由希腊语构件 micro- 与 bio- 拼成，英语又用 microbial、microbiology 与 microbicide 加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Greek mikros means small, and the combining form bio- comes from bios, life; the final -e marks a French spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 mikros 意为微小，组合构词形式 bio- 来自 bios（生命）；词尾 -e 带有法语拼写的痕迹。

items.example: The prefix micro- forms microscope.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 micro- 构成 microscope。

items.example: Bios is the life element in the word.
items.exampleCN: bios 是这个词里的「生命」构件。

items.example: The form bio- forms biology.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 bio- 构成 biology。

items.example: Microbe was coined in French.
items.exampleCN: microbe 是在法语中造出的。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms microbial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 microbial。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms microbic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 microbic。

items.example: The form -logy forms microbiology.
items.exampleCN: 组合词 -logy 构成 microbiology。

items.example: The form -cide forms microbicide.
items.exampleCN: 组合词 -cide 构成 microbicide。

items.example: Microbiology studies invisible life.
items.exampleCN: microbiology 研究看不见的生命。

definition_zh: 微博；微博客；在微博上发布的短讯
definition_en: a blog that uses very short posts, usually one or two sentences, and lets people follow and reply to them
core_image: 屏幕上一行行短得只够说一句话的帖子，飞速刷过
scene: 地铁上，女孩一边听歌一边点开手机，把自己刚想好的几句话发到自己的小博客上，几秒后就有朋友来评论。She posts a short thought on her microblog every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 microblog 是「微博、微博客」（第 1 个义项：篇幅极短、关注与回复都很快的博客）；句意：她每天早上都在自己的微博上发一句简短的想法。

derivatives.zh: microblog 加 -er 构成，义为写微博的人
microblog 加 -ing 构成，义为写微博这项活动
过去分词兼作形容词，义为在微博上发布过的

senses.title: A blog of very short posts
senses.definition: a blog in which users publish very short text posts for a wide audience
senses.definitionCN: 用户向广大读者发布极短文字帖子的博客
senses.example: Her microblog has half a million readers.
senses.exampleCN: 她的微博有五十万读者。
senses.why: Micro- trims the old word blog down to its smallest form, so a microblog is a blog with the text cut short.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 micro- 把旧词 blog 削到最小形态，所以 microblog 就是「文字被裁短的博客」。

senses.title: One short post itself
senses.definition: a single short message posted on such a service
senses.definitionCN: 在这类服务上发布的一条简短讯息
senses.example: He deleted the microblog ten minutes after sending it.
senses.exampleCN: 他发出那条微博十分钟后就删掉了。
senses.why: As with blog, the name of the medium drifts onto each single item placed in it.
senses.whyCN: 和 blog 一样，媒介的名称会漂移到放入其中的每一条内容上。

senses.title: To post very short updates
senses.definition: to publish brief updates on such a service
senses.definitionCN: 在这种服务上发布简短的更新
senses.example: Fans microblogged the news within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝们在几秒内就把消息发上了微博。
senses.why: Once a noun names an activity, it easily becomes a verb for doing that activity.
senses.whyCN: 一个名词一旦命名某项活动，就很容易被用作动词来表示从事这项活动。

intro.en: Microblog joins the Greek small element micro- to the word blog, which is a shortened web log.
intro.cn: microblog 把希腊语中表示微小的 micro- 加在 blog 上，而 blog 是 web log 的缩写。

items.en: Weblog names a personal site of dated posts.
items.cn: 二十世纪九十年代 weblog 指按日期排列帖子的个人网站。

items.en: Blog appears as a clipped form of weblog.
items.cn: 一九九九年 blog 作为 weblog 的截短形式出现。

items.en: Micro- still means small in compounds.
items.cn: 在复合词中 micro- 仍表示微小。

items.en: Microblog labels blogging trimmed to short posts.
items.cn: 二十一世纪初 microblog 指被裁成短帖的博客。

items.en: The word also serves as a verb.
items.cn: 这个词如今也用作动词。

note.en: Microblog shares the micro- family with microphone and microscope, and sits beside other short-message tools.
note.cn: microblog 与 microphone、microscope 同属 micro- 词族，并与其它短讯工具相邻。

entries.definition: a person who writes a microblog
the activity of writing short posts
a device that picks up sound
entries.definitionCN: 麦克风：拾取声音的装置

entries.definition: an online diary of written posts
entries.definitionCN: 博客：按时间发布文章的网上日志

entries.definition: a short message about what someone is doing
entries.definitionCN: 状态更新：一句关于近况的短讯

entries.definition: a message placed online

normalIntro.en: Microblog is a visible compound: small plus blog, with the Greek micro- doing the shrinking.
normalIntro.cn: microblog 是一个看得见结构的复合词：微小 + 博客，由希腊语 micro- 负责「缩小」。

normal.en: Micro- shrinks anything, as in microphone and microscope.
normal.cn: 前缀 micro- 能把任何东西缩小，如 microphone 与 microscope。

normal.en: Blog itself is a clipped form of web log.
normal.cn: blog 本身就是 web log 的截短形式。

normal.en: Add -er and you get a microblogger, the person behind the short posts.
normal.cn: 加上 -er 得到 microblogger，指那些发布短帖的人。

normal.en: Add -ing and you get microblogging, the activity of the whole network.
normal.cn: 加上 -ing 得到 microblogging，指整个网络上的这项活动。

normal.en: Compare blog and microblog: a blog has long posts, a microblog has a few words.
