normal.cn: 对比 blog 与 microblog：博客帖子长，微博只有几个字。

abstract.en: Picture a blog that has been shrunk to fit a phone screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被缩小到刚好放进手机屏幕的博客。

abstract.en: Imagine a sentence sent to a million screens at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话在同一瞬间送往百万块屏幕。

abstract.en: Think of a stream of tiny notes, one after another.
abstract.cn: 想象一连串短小的字条，一张接一张滑过。

examples.en: The company posts its latest offers on its microblog.
examples.cn: 公司把自己的最新优惠发布在微博上。

examples.en: Thousands of fans microblogged about the concert all night.
examples.cn: 成千上万的粉丝整晚都在微博上谈论这场演唱会。

examples.en: A short microblog can spread faster than a long article.
examples.cn: 一条短微博传播起来比一篇长文更快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈克罗博客」——micro 是「微小」，blog 是「博客」，合起来就是「微小的博客」；这只是拆字联想，与词源构词有关但并非历史演变。

root: micro-（希腊语 mikros，微小）+ blog（web log 的截短形式）→ 英语 microblog（二十一世纪初新造），核心义「被缩小为短帖的博客」。

sensesIntro.en: Microblog names the platform first, then a single post, and finally the act of posting.
sensesIntro.cn: microblog 先指平台，再指一条帖子，最后指发帖这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blog squeezed down to one line on a phone.
core.cn: 核心意象：被压到手机上只有一行的博客。

branches.en: The platform sense describes the service.
branches.cn: 平台义项描述这项服务。

branches.en: The item sense points at one post.
branches.cn: 条目义项指向单独一条帖子。

branches.en: The verb sense covers the act of posting.
branches.cn: 动词义项覆盖发帖这个动作。

branches.en: The platform is made of its posts.
branches.cn: 平台由一条条帖子构成。

branches.en: A post is the result of posting.
branches.cn: 一条帖子正是发帖的结果。

intro.en: Microblog is a transparent compound of the prefix micro- and the clipped noun blog.
intro.cn: microblog 是前缀 micro- 与截短名词 blog 组合而成的透明复合词。

latinIntro.en: Micro- comes from Greek mikros, small; blog is a modern clipping of web log, so the word has no single Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: micro- 来自希腊语 mikros（小）；blog 是现代英语对 web log 的截短，因此这个词没有单一的拉丁词根。

items.example: The prefix micro- forms microblog.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 micro- 构成 microblog。

items.example: Mikros is the source of micro-.
items.exampleCN: mikros 是 micro- 的来源。

items.example: Log survives inside blog.
items.exampleCN: log 保留在 blog 内部。

items.example: Blog is the base of microblog.
items.exampleCN: blog 是 microblog 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms microblogger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 microblogger。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms microblogging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 microblogging。

items.meaningCN: 表示过去式或过去分词的词尾
items.example: The ending -ed forms microblogged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 microblogged。

items.meaning: a person who writes short posts
items.example: Microbloggers post from their phones.
items.exampleCN: 微博作者用手机发帖。

items.example: Microblogging grew fast after 2006.
items.exampleCN: 写微博这项活动在二〇〇六年之后迅速兴起。

definition_zh: 微观世界；缩影；小宇宙
definition_en: a small place, group, or system that contains all the features of a much larger one
core_image: 一滴池水被放大，无数微小生物在其中自成世界
scene: 池里的一滴水和整个大湖几乎一模一样。A drop of pond water is a microcosm of the whole lake.
sceneCN: 这里 microcosm 是「缩影」（第 1 个义项：小规模却包含大世界全部特征的整体）；句意：池里的一滴水和整个大湖几乎一模一样。

derivatives.zh: 微观世界的；缩影式的（由 microcosm 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成）
宏观世界；大宇宙（把前缀 micro- 换成 macro- 后的对照词）
以缩影的方式（由 microcosmic 加 -ally 构成，较少用）

senses.title: A small world reflecting a larger one
senses.definition: a small place, group, or system that shows all the features of a much larger one
senses.definitionCN: 规模很小、却包含更大整体全部特征的地方、群体或系统
senses.example: The village is a microcosm of the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄是整个国家的缩影。
senses.why: Greek mikros kosmos means a little world, so the image of a complete world held inside a small space is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mikros kosmos 意为「小世界」，所以「小空间里装着一个完整世界」的画面本就在词里。

senses.title: The miniature form of something
senses.definition: something presented on a very small scale but showing the same pattern as the full version
senses.definitionCN: 以极小的规模呈现、却与完整版本模式相同的事物
senses.example: The exhibition shows the city in microcosm.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览以微缩形式展现了这座城市。
senses.why: Because the small world repeats the large one, it can stand in for it as a model seen at reduced scale.
senses.whyCN: 因为小世界重复着大世界，所以它能以缩小比例充当大世界的模型。

senses.title: A self-contained little universe
senses.titleCN: 小宇宙；自成一体的小天地
senses.definition: a small, self-contained world of its own, especially in philosophy or religion
senses.definitionCN: 自成一体的小天地，多用于哲学或宗教语境
senses.example: The old city is a microcosm cut off from the modern world.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古城是一个与现代世界隔绝的小天地。
senses.why: Philosophy set the little world against the great world, so the word also names any small enclosed sphere of life.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「小世界」与「大世界」相对，于是这个词也指任何封闭的小生活圈。

senses.title: The illustrated version of a larger pattern
senses.definition: a group or case whose features illustrate the general pattern of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 特征足以说明更大整体普遍规律的小群体或个案
senses.example: That one project is a microcosm of how the company works.
senses.exampleCN: 那个项目正是公司运作方式的缩影。
senses.why: When a case repeats a large pattern, writers use the word to say one small example explains the whole picture.
senses.whyCN: 当个案重复着大格局时，作者用这个词表示「一个小例子就能说明全貌」。

intro.en: Microcosm joins Greek mikros, meaning small, with Greek kosmos, meaning order or world.
intro.cn: microcosm 由希腊语 mikros（小的）与 kosmos（秩序、世界）组合而成。

items.en: Mikros means small and kosmos means order, arrangement, or world.
items.cn: mikros 意为「小的」，kosmos 意为「秩序、安排、世界」。

items.en: Philosophers used the idea of a little world mirroring a great world.
items.cn: 哲学家提出「小世界映照大世界」的观念。

items.en: The compound microcosmus enters Latin learning.
items.cn: 复合词 microcosmus 进入拉丁语学术传统。

items.en: English writers adopt microcosm to describe the human body and the earth.
items.cn: 英语作者采用 microcosm，用来指人体与地球这类「小世界」。

items.en: The word is extended to any small system, such as a society or a habitat.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到任何小系统，如某个社会或生境。

note.en: Microcosm belongs to a small family of -cosm words, and its near meanings are words for small-scale models and examples.
note.cn: microcosm 属于以 -cosm 结尾的一小族词，近义场则是表示微缩模型与实例的词。

entries.definition: the whole large universe seen as a single system
relating to a small world or shown in miniature
the universe as an ordered whole
a very small copy of something
entries.definitionCN: 缩微模型；极小的复制品

entries.definition: a perfect example of a quality or type
a small part taken to represent the whole

normalIntro.en: Microcosm is a little kosmos, a world in miniature, so remember micro for small and cosm for world.
normalIntro.cn: microcosm 就是一个小小的 kosmos，即微缩的世界；记住 micro 表示「小」、cosm 表示「世界」。

normal.en: The prefix micro- means very small.
normal.cn: 前缀 micro- 表示「极小」。

normal.en: The root cosm appears in cosmos and cosmic.
normal.cn: 词根 cosm 也出现在 cosmos 与 cosmic 中。

normal.en: A microcosm of something means a small copy of the whole.
normal.cn: a microcosm of 某事物 就是该事物的缩小版。

normal.en: In microcosm means shown on a very small scale.
normal.cn: in microcosm 表示以微缩的形式展现。

normal.en: Macrocosm is the opposite partner: macro- means large.
normal.cn: macrocosm 是它的对照词：macro- 表示「大」。

abstract.en: Picture a snow globe holding a tiny city inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个水晶球，里面装着一座小小的城市。

abstract.en: Think of a model village that copies every street of the real town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个模型村庄，把真实城镇的每条街都复制下来。

abstract.en: Imagine glancing at an old city and seeing a whole world sealed inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象你望着一座古城，仿佛看见一个完整世界被封存在里面。

examples.en: The festival is a microcosm of many urban cultures.
examples.cn: 这个节日是这座城市多元文化的缩影。

examples.en: These small coral habitats show the ocean in microcosm.
examples.cn: 这些小型珊瑚生境以微缩形式展现了海洋。

examples.en: Her diary offers a microcosm of life during the war.
examples.cn: 她的日记提供了战时生活的一个缩影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克若小宇宙」——麦克风一照，小宇宙就浮现；谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小的）+ kosmos（秩序、世界）→ 中世纪拉丁语 microcosmus → 英语 microcosm，核心义「装在小小空间里的完整世界」。

sensesIntro.en: Microcosm begins as a little world that mirrors a great one, then covers any miniature form, any self-contained sphere, and any case that illustrates a larger pattern.
sensesIntro.cn: microcosm 最初指映照大世界的小世界，随后扩展为微缩形式、自成一体的小天地，以及能说明大格局的典型个案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water holding a whole world of tiny life.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴水里装着一整个微小生命的世界。

branches.en: A small world that reflects a large one is the central sense.
branches.cn: 映照大世界的小世界是核心义项。

branches.en: The miniature form sense stresses the reduced scale.
branches.cn: 微缩形式义强调比例的缩小。

branches.en: The self-contained little universe sense comes from philosophy.
branches.cn: 自成一体的小天地义来自哲学语境。

branches.en: A typical case works because it repeats the larger pattern.
branches.cn: 典型实例之所以成立，是因为它重复了大格局。

branches.en: All three senses rest on the idea that a small part shows the whole.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都建立在「小部分显出整体」的想法上。

intro.en: Microcosm is built from the prefix micro- and the combining form -cosm, with macrocosm as its partner word.
intro.cn: microcosm 由前缀 micro- 与组合成分 -cosm 构成，其对照词是 macrocosm。

latinIntro.en: The parts come from Greek mikros and kosmos, which passed into Latin learning as microcosmus.
latinIntro.cn: 各部分来自希腊语 mikros 与 kosmos，并以 microcosmus 的形式传入拉丁语学术传统。

items.example: The prefix micro- appears in microscope and microchip.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 micro- 出现在 microscope 与 microchip 中。

items.example: Mikros supplies the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: mikros 提供这个词的前半部分。

items.example: Kosmos supplies the world half of the word.
items.exampleCN: kosmos 提供「世界」这一半。

items.example: The combining form -cosm appears in phrases such as macrocosm.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -cosm 也出现在 macrocosm 之中。

items.example: The prefix macro- gives the matching word macrocosm.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 macro- 构成对应的 macrocosm。

items.example: Macrocosm names the large world that the small one mirrors.
items.exampleCN: macrocosm 指小世界所映照的大世界。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms the adjective microcosmic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成形容词 microcosmic。

items.example: Microcosmic describes things seen on a tiny scale.
items.exampleCN: microcosmic 描述以微小尺度呈现的事物。

definition_zh: 微处理器；微处理机
definition_en: a single small chip that carries out the instructions and calculations of a computer
core_image: 一枚指甲盖大小的芯片，里面排着密密麻麻的电路
scene: 手机里那枚小小的芯片负责所有运算。The microprocessor inside the phone handles every calculation.
sceneCN: 这里 microprocessor 是「微处理器」（第 1 个义项：一块芯片承担计算机的全部指令与运算）；句意：手机里那枚小小的芯片负责所有运算。

derivatives.zh: 微处理（由 microprocessor 加后缀 -ing 构成）
基于微处理器的（由 microprocessor 加 -based 构成的复合形容词）
处理器（去掉前缀 micro- 后的基础词）
微芯片；芯片（同属微电子词族）

senses.title: A single chip that runs a computer
senses.definition: a single small chip that handles the instructions and calculations of a computer or similar device
senses.definitionCN: 一块小芯片，完成计算机或类似设备的指令处理与运算
senses.example: This laptop uses a faster microprocessor than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这台笔记本电脑用的微处理器比旧的那台更快。
senses.why: Micro- means small and processor comes from Latin pro- forward and cedere to go, so the word is a small chip that carries instructions forward.
senses.whyCN: micro- 表示「小」，processor 源自拉丁语 pro-（向前）与 cedere（行进），所以这个词就是「推动指令向前走的小芯片」。

senses.title: The chip that integrates the central unit
senses.definition: the integrated circuit that combines the main computing units of a computer on one piece of silicon
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机主要计算单元集成在一块硅片上的集成电路
senses.example: The first microprocessor put an entire central unit on one chip.
senses.exampleCN: 最早的微处理器把整个中央处理单元放在一块芯片上。
senses.why: The invention of the integrated circuit replaced large racks of parts with one unit, and micro- marks that huge reduction in size.
senses.whyCN: 集成电路的出现把成排的大型器件换成单一部件，前缀 micro- 正标记了这种体积上的巨大缩小。

senses.title: The control unit inside everyday machines
senses.definition: a small control chip built into an everyday device such as a car, a washing machine, or a camera
senses.definitionCN: 装在汽车、洗衣机、相机等日常设备里的小型控制芯片
senses.example: The car has several microprocessors that regulate fuel use.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车有几个微处理器，用来调节燃油使用。
senses.why: Because the chip is small and cheap, it can be hidden inside machines that never look like computers.
senses.whyCN: 因为芯片小而便宜，它可以藏在那些看起来根本不像计算机的机器里。

senses.title: The core of the information age
senses.titleCN: 微处理器时代；信息技术核心
senses.definition: the technology seen as the driving force of modern computing and digital change
senses.definitionCN: 被视为现代计算与数字化变革驱动力的技术
senses.example: The microprocessor changed how people work and communicate.
senses.exampleCN: 微处理器改变了人们工作和沟通的方式。
senses.why: When a new chip changes many industries at once, its name becomes a shorthand for the whole technological shift.
senses.whyCN: 当一种新芯片同时改变许多行业时，它的名字就成了整场技术变革的代称。

intro.en: Microprocessor combines the Greek prefix micro-, meaning small, with the English word processor, from Latin procedere, to go forward.
intro.cn: microprocessor 由希腊语前缀 micro-（小的）与英语词 processor（源自拉丁语 procedere，意为向前行进）合成。

items.en: Cedere means to go or yield, and procedere means to go forward.
items.cn: cedere 意为「行进、让出」，procedere 意为「向前行进」。

items.en: Process grows into the noun form used for handling materials and information.
items.cn: process 逐步发展出表示处理材料与信息的名词用法。

items.en: The suffix -or forms processor, the thing that carries out processing.
items.cn: 后缀 -or 构成 processor，指执行处理的事物。

items.en: Engineers attach micro- to describe a processor built on one chip.
items.cn: 工程师把 micro- 加在前面，用来描述做在一枚芯片上的处理器。

items.en: The term spreads with the first single-chip central units in calculators and personal computers.
items.cn: 随着计算器与个人计算机中单芯片中央单元的出现，这个说法迅速传播开来。

note.en: Microprocessor sits close to the -chip family on the form side and to the processing and computing words on the meaning side.
note.cn: microprocessor 在形式上靠近以 chip 为核心的一族词，在意义上则与处理、计算类词相近。

entries.definition: a device or program that processes data
a tiny electronic circuit on a silicon chip
the design and making of very small electronic circuits
a small piece of silicon holding an electronic circuit
the main part of a computer that runs instructions
entries.definitionCN: 中央处理器（计算机执行指令的主要部件）

entries.definition: a complete circuit built on one small piece of material

normalIntro.en: Microprocessor makes sense as a small subject and an action-holder: micro is tiny, process is to carry through, and -or is the thing that does it.
normalIntro.cn: microprocessor 可以拆成「小而做事的主体」来记：micro 是微小，process 是处理，-or 指做事的东西。

normal.en: Micro- means small, as in microscope and microphone.
normal.cn: micro- 表示「小」，如 microscope 与 microphone。

normal.en: The word processor names the part that processes data.
normal.cn: processor 指处理数据的部件。

normal.en: A suffix -or often marks the doer or the device.
normal.cn: 后缀 -or 常标记施动者或装置。

normal.en: A microprocessor chip means the silicon piece itself.
normal.cn: a microprocessor chip 指的就是那块硅片本身。

normal.en: Processor means the general case while the micro version is the small single chip.
normal.cn: processor 泛指处理器，加上 micro 后的版本专指小型单芯片。

abstract.en: Picture a chip the size of a fingernail doing the work of a room of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚指甲大小的芯片，干着过去一屋子机器才干的话。

abstract.en: Imagine a city gate that lets every instruction pass through in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道城门，让每条指令依次通过。

abstract.en: Think of a tiny brain hidden inside a car or a camera.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小小的「大脑」藏在汽车或相机里面。

examples.en: Engineers designed a microprocessor that uses very little power.
examples.cn: 工程师设计了一款功耗极低的微处理器。

examples.en: New microprocessors made personal computers cheap enough for homes.
examples.cn: 新型微处理器让人人家里都买得起个人电脑。

examples.en: The device fails if the microprocessor overheats.
examples.cn: 如果微处理器过热，这台设备就会失灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克若处理器」——麦克风旁边那枚小芯片在悄悄处理一切；谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小的）→ 前缀 micro- + 拉丁语 procedere（向前行进）→ process（处理）+ 后缀 -or → processor，合起来指「一枚小芯片承担全部处理工作」。

sensesIntro.en: Microprocessor first names one chip that runs a computer, then the integrated central unit, then the hidden control chip in everyday machines, and finally the whole computing era.
sensesIntro.cn: microprocessor 先指一枚执行计算机处理的芯片，再指集成的中央单元，然后指隐藏在日常设备里的控制芯片，最后指整个计算时代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingernail-sized chip crowded with fine circuits.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚指甲盖大小、布满细密电路的芯片。

branches.en: The core sense is a single chip that runs calculations.
branches.cn: 核心义项是执行运算的单一芯片。

branches.en: The integrated sense stresses that one piece of silicon holds the whole central unit.
branches.cn: 集成义强调一整块硅片容纳整个中央单元。

branches.en: The embedded sense moves the chip into everyday machines.
branches.cn: 嵌入式义项把芯片放进日常机器。

branches.en: The era sense uses the chip to name a broad technological change.
branches.cn: 时代义用这枚芯片来命名一场广泛的技术变革。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the same reduction: a room of parts squeezed onto one chip.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都依赖同一种收缩：一屋子部件被压缩到一枚芯片上。

intro.en: Microprocessor joins the productive prefix micro- with the agent noun processor, and the family includes microchip and processor.
intro.cn: microprocessor 把构词力强的前缀 micro- 与施动名词 processor 结合，同族词包括 microchip 与 processor。

latinIntro.en: The meaningful parts trace back to Greek mikros, meaning small, and Latin procedere, meaning to go forward.
latinIntro.cn: 各意义单元可追溯到希腊语 mikros（小的）与拉丁语 procedere（向前行进）。

items.example: The prefix micro- marks a very small scale.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 micro- 标记极小的尺度。

items.example: The prefix pro- appears in proceed and process.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 出现在 proceed 与 process 中。

items.example: Cedere is the old verb behind proceed.
items.exampleCN: cedere 是 proceed 背后的古老动词。

items.meaning: a series of actions; to handle data
items.example: Process covers both a series of steps and the handling of data.
items.exampleCN: process 既指一系列步骤，也指处理数据。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.meaningCN: 做某事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -or forms processor and operator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 processor 与 operator。

items.example: Processor names any device that processes data.
items.exampleCN: processor 指处理数据的装置。

items.meaning: a processor built on one chip
items.example: Microprocessor puts the whole processor on one chip.
items.exampleCN: microprocessor 把整个处理器放到一枚芯片上。

items.example: Microchip shares the micro- prefix and the chip idea.
items.exampleCN: microchip 共享 micro- 前缀与芯片概念。

items.example: The suffix -based forms microprocessor-based.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -based 构成 microprocessor-based。

latinEntries.meaning: one who brings forward or advances

definition_zh: 微波；微波炉；用微波炉加热
definition_en: a very short radio wave, the oven that cooks with such waves, or to cook food in it
core_image: 一个箱子里，看不见的短波让水分子剧烈晃动、食物变热
scene: 午饭只有一份冷掉的米饭，放进炉子里转两分钟就好。The cold rice only needs two minutes in the microwave.
sceneCN: 这里 microwave 是「微波炉」（第 2 个义项：用微波加热食物的电器）；句意：冷掉的米饭只需要在微波炉里放两分钟。

pos.zh: 用微波炉加热；微波加热

derivatives.zh: 可用微波加热的（由 microwave 加后缀 -able 构成）
小孢子（同为 micro- 前缀构成的科学术语，仅作构词类比）
波长（由 wave 加 length 构成，与 wave 同族）

senses.title: A very short radio wave
senses.definition: a radio wave with a very short wavelength, used for heating, radar, and communication
senses.definitionCN: 波长极短的无线电波，用于加热、雷达与通信
senses.example: Radar sends out microwave signals to detect distant planes.
senses.exampleCN: 雷达发出微波信号来探测远处的飞机。
senses.why: The word is simply micro short plus wave a wave, so a microwave is a wave much shorter than the ordinary radio waves known at the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 micro（短的）加上 wave（波），所以微波就是比当时常见无线电波短得多的那一类波。

senses.title: The oven that heats food
senses.definition: an oven that cooks or heats food quickly using microwaves
senses.definitionCN: 用微波快速加热或烹调食物的炉子
senses.example: She warmed the soup in the microwave.
senses.exampleCN: 她用微波炉热了汤。
senses.why: Because microwaves make the water inside food get hot, the machine that produces them took the wave name as its own.
senses.whyCN: 因为微波能让食物里的水变热，产生这种波的电器就顺理成章地用了「微波」这个名字。

senses.title: To heat food with microwaves
senses.definition: to cook or heat food in a microwave oven
senses.definitionCN: 用微波炉烹调或加热食物
senses.example: Microwave the pie for one minute on high.
senses.exampleCN: 把馅饼用高火微波一分钟。
senses.why: As with many device nouns, the oven name turned into a verb that names the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 和许多表示器械的名词一样，微波炉的名字也转化为动词，表示「使用它」这个动作。

senses.title: The heating method itself
senses.definition: the method of heating by high-frequency waves, as in cooking or laboratory use
senses.definitionCN: 以高频波加热的方法，用于烹调或实验
senses.example: This method of heating is sometimes called microwave heating.
senses.exampleCN: 这种加热方式有时被称为微波加热。
senses.why: Once the effect was understood, the wave name came to label the process, not just the wave or the oven.
senses.whyCN: 弄清加热原理之后，这个波名又被用来标示加热过程，而不只是波本身或炉子。

intro.en: Microwave is an English compound of the prefix micro-, meaning short or small, and the noun wave.
intro.cn: microwave 是英语复合词，由前缀 micro-（短、小）与名词 wave（波）构成。

items.en: The prefix goes back to Greek mikros, meaning small.
items.cn: 前缀可追溯到希腊语 mikros，意为小的。

items.en: The word wave refers to a raised ridge on water and to the motion of light.
items.cn: wave 既指水面隆起的波峰，也指光的波动。

items.en: Physicists name electromagnetic waves short enough to fall below ordinary radio waves.
items.cn: 物理学家把短于普通无线电波的电磁波命名为一种短波。

items.en: Microwave radar and microwave ovens popularise the everyday use for the oven.
items.cn: 微波雷达与微波炉让「微波炉」这一日常义项普及开来。

items.en: The noun produces the verb to describe heating food in such an oven.
items.cn: 该名词随后产生动词用法，表示用这种炉子加热食物。

note.en: Microwave shares its building blocks with a wave family and sits close to a set of kitchen heating words.
note.cn: microwave 与 wave 一族共享构词成分，在意义上又靠近一组厨房加热用语。

entries.definition: an instrument for looking at very small objects
entries.definitionCN: 显微镜（同用 micro- 前缀，但词源不同）

entries.definition: the distance between two points on a wave
having curves like waves
an enclosed space that heats food
an appliance with hot surfaces for cooking
to heat food again before eating

normalIntro.en: Microwave can be read as micro plus wave, a tiny wave that heats food and, by extension, the oven and the act of heating.
normalIntro.cn: microwave 可读作 micro 加 wave，即「很短的波」，能加热食物，继而指炉子和加热动作。

normal.en: Micro- means small, so microwaves are short waves.
normal.cn: micro- 表示「小」，所以微波是短的波。

normal.en: Microwave oven is the full name of the kitchen machine.
normal.cn: microwave oven 是这种厨房电器的全称。

normal.en: Put it in the microwave is the most common everyday phrase.
normal.cn: put it in the microwave 是日常最高频的说法。

normal.en: Microwave-safe marks boxes that will not melt.
normal.cn: microwave-safe 标记那些不会熔化的餐盒。

normal.en: Compare oven and stove: oven has a door, stove has burners.
normal.cn: 对比 oven 与 stove：oven 带门，stove 带灶眼。

abstract.en: Picture invisible short waves shaking the water inside a potato.
abstract.cn: 想象看不见的短波让土豆里的水分子剧烈晃动。

abstract.en: Think of a closed box with a small window and a spinning plate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带小窗口、里面有转盘的封闭箱子。

abstract.en: Imagine a plate of cold pasta steaming after one short burst.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘冷意面在短短一发加热后冒起热气。

examples.en: He microwaved his lunch instead of waiting for the cafe line.
examples.cn: 他没去咖啡馆排队，而是用微波炉热了午饭。

examples.en: Do not put metal forks into the microwave.
examples.cn: 不要把金属叉子放进微波炉。

examples.en: Microwaves carry phone signals over long distances.
examples.cn: 微波可以远距离传输电话信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克若喂」——麦克风一响，冷饭就被喂进炉子里热好了；谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小的）→ 英语前缀 micro- + 英语名词 wave（波）→ microwave（短波）→ 由波名转指微波炉，再转为动词「用微波加热」。

sensesIntro.en: Microwave starts as a short electromagnetic wave, then names the oven that uses such waves, the verb for heating food in it, and finally the heating method itself.
sensesIntro.cn: microwave 最初指短波，随后指使用这种波的炉子，再转为「用炉子加热食物」的动词，最后指这种加热方法本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: invisible short waves making the water in food move and heat up.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的短波让食物里的水晃动升温。

branches.en: The scientific sense names the short electromagnetic wave.
branches.cn: 科学义项指这种短波电磁波。

branches.en: The oven sense shifts the name from the wave to the machine.
branches.cn: 微波炉义把名字从波转到机器上。

branches.en: The verb sense turns the machine into an action.
branches.cn: 动词义把机器变成动作。

branches.en: The method sense names the heating process itself.
branches.cn: 加热方法义指加热过程本身。

branches.en: The oven and the verb are two sides of the same everyday action.
branches.cn: 微波炉与动词义是同一个日常动作的两面。

intro.en: Microwave is a modern English compound: the prefix micro- carries shortness, and the free word wave carries the wave.
intro.cn: microwave 是英语现代复合词：前缀 micro- 表示「短」，自由词 wave 表示「波」。

latinIntro.en: The first element traces to Greek mikros, meaning small, while wave is a native English word of uncertain older origin.
latinIntro.cn: 第一个成分可追溯到希腊语 mikros（小的），而 wave 是本土英语词，更早的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix micro- appears in microwave and microscope.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 micro- 出现在 microwave 与 microscope 中。

items.example: Mikros is the Greek source of micro-.
items.exampleCN: mikros 是 micro- 的希腊语来源。

items.meaning: a moving ridge or a vibration
items.example: Wave names both sea ridges and vibrations.
items.exampleCN: wave 既指海浪也指振动。

items.example: Microwave joins the short marker to the wave word.
items.exampleCN: microwave 把表示短的成分与 wave 结合。

items.example: Microwave oven makes the wave name into a device name.
items.exampleCN: microwave oven 把波名变成器械名。

items.example: The suffix -able forms microwaveable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 microwaveable。

items.meaning: the length of one wave cycle
items.example: Wavelength pairs wave with the noun length.
items.exampleCN: wavelength 把 wave 与 length 组合。

items.example: Microscope shares the prefix but names a different device.
items.exampleCN: microscope 共享同一前缀，但指另一种器械。

definition_zh: 中间；中央；正当中
definition_en: the middle part of a place, a group, or an event
core_image: 被一圈人和事围在正中间的那个人
scene: 集市上人声鼎沸，她站在人群正当中，抬头寻找同伴。She stood in the midst of the bustling crowd and looked up to find her friend.
sceneCN: 这里 midst 是「当中、中间」（第 1 个义项：人群或地方的正中间）；句意：她站在熙攘人群的正当中，抬头寻找同伴。

collocations.zh: 在我们中间；就在我们身边

collocations.phrase: in the midst of a crisis
in the midst of the crowd

derivatives.zh: 由同一个古英语「中间」词干演变而来，义为「中间；中部」
在古英语阶段由「在……当中」的介词短语固化而成，义为「在……之中」
amid 加 -st 的变体，义为「在……当中」，与 midst 同属一组

senses.title: The middle of a place or group
senses.definition: the central part of a place or the position between other people
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方的中心部位，或夹在其他人之中的位置
senses.example: A small fountain stood in the midst of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场正中央立着一座小喷泉。
senses.why: The word began as a noun for the middle point, so the physical centre is its oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就表示空间的中点，所以「正中间」是最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: Being among people
senses.definition: the state of being surrounded by other people
senses.definitionCN: 被人群包围、处在众人之间的状态
senses.example: The spy had lived in our midst for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个间谍多年来一直生活在我们中间。
senses.why: If something is in the middle, it is among the others, so midst came to describe being surrounded by people.
senses.whyCN: 某物在中间，也就是处在其他事物之间，于是 midst 引申为「身处人群之中」。

senses.title: The middle period of an event
senses.definition: the middle part of a period or process, especially a difficult one
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间或过程的中间阶段，尤指困难的时期
senses.example: He called during the midst of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他是在暴风雨正猛的时候打来电话的。
senses.why: The centre of time works like the centre of space, so the word also names the middle of an event.
senses.whyCN: 时间的中心与空间的中心同理，因此这个词也用来指事件进行到一半的阶段。

senses.title: While doing something
senses.definition: in the course of an activity that is still going on
senses.definitionCN: 在仍在进行的某项活动中
senses.example: She left in the midst of writing her report.
senses.exampleCN: 她报告写到一半就离开了。
senses.why: The fixed phrase in the midst of extended the middle to an unfinished action, meaning partway through it.
senses.whyCN: 固定短语 in the midst of 把「中间」扩展到未完成的动作上，表示「做到一半」。

intro.en: Midst goes back to Old English midd, the middle, and the ending -st, which marks a place or state.
intro.cn: midst 可追溯至古英语 midd（中间），加上表示地点或状态的词尾 -st。

items.en: Middest appears as a superlative-style form meaning the middle one.
items.cn: middest 以最高级形式出现，意为「最当中的」。

items.en: Emiddes acts as a preposition meaning in the middle of.
items.cn: emiddes 用作介词，意为「在……中间」。

items.en: The word is shortened to middes and amidde.
items.cn: 词形缩短为 middes 与 amidde。

items.en: Midst settles as the noun, and amidst keeps the preposition role.
items.cn: midst 固定为名词，amidst 保留介词角色。

items.en: In the midst of becomes the dominant fixed phrase.
items.cn: in the midst of 成为最主要的固定搭配。

note.en: Midst shares its stem with middle, amid, and amidst, and sits close to centre words.
note.cn: midst 与 middle、amid、amidst 共享词干，并与表示「中心」的词语意义相邻。

entries.definition: the central point of a space
in the middle of something
a longer form of amid
entries.definitionCN: amid 的加长形式，与 midst 同属一族，义为「在……当中」

entries.definition: the exact middle point
the central part of something
crowded together, as in the thick of things
entries.definitionCN: 在 thick of things 中同样表示「最忙、最密集的中心」，只是拼写相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Midst is the middle seen as a place: a spot surrounded on every side.
normalIntro.cn: midst 就是把「中间」看成一个地点：四面都被围住的那一处。

normal.en: In the midst of means in the middle of.
normal.cn: in the midst of 意为「在……当中」。

normal.en: Keep the word in an article: in our midst means among us.
normal.cn: 连上冠词记 in our midst，意思就是「在我们中间」。

normal.en: Compare middle and amid, which share the same ancient stem.
normal.cn: 对比 middle 与 amid，它们共享同一个古老词干。

normal.en: Use midst for a place, a group, or an event, not for a single object.
normal.cn: midst 用于地方、人群或事件，不用于单个物体。

normal.en: Midst is slightly formal and literary; in speech many people say in the middle of.
normal.cn: midst 略显正式且有文学味；口语里人们常说 in the middle of。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing in the exact centre of a circle of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人正好站在一圈朋友的正中央。

abstract.en: Imagine a stranger sitting quietly in the middle of a family dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人在家庭聚餐的正中间安静坐着。

abstract.en: See a storm cloud right overhead with thunder on all sides.
abstract.cn: 想象乌云正压在头顶，四周都是雷声。

examples.en: In the midst of the crowd, I lost sight of my sister.
examples.cn: 在人群当中，我看不见我妹妹了。

examples.en: The village was hit by a flood in the midst of winter.
examples.cn: 村子在隆冬时节遭遇了洪水。

examples.en: A quiet hero lived in their midst for many years.
examples.cn: 一位默默无闻的英雄在他们中间生活了许多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米得死特」太拗口，不如想一想：一堆「米」堆成小山，人站到正中间——这就是 midst；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 midd（中间）+ 词尾 -st → 中古英语 middes → 英语 midst，核心义「四面被围住的正中间」。

sensesIntro.en: Midst starts with a physical centre, moves to standing among people, then to the middle of an event and a fixed phrase for an action in progress.
sensesIntro.cn: midst 先指空间上的正中，再引申为身处人群之中，进而指事件进行到一半，最后固化为表示动作进行中的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the exact centre, surrounded on every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在正中央，四面都被围住。

branches.en: The physical centre is the most literal branch.
branches.cn: 空间上的正中是最字面的分支。

branches.en: The social branch describes being among a group of people.
branches.cn: 社会层面的分支表示身处一群人当中。

branches.en: The temporal branch moves the centre from space onto time.
branches.cn: 时间分支把「中心」从空间移到了时间上。

branches.en: The phrase in the midst of links the middle to an unfinished action.
branches.cn: 短语 in the midst of 把「中间」与未完成的动作联系起来。

branches.en: Both the square and the crowd place the subject inside a surrounding whole.
branches.cn: 无论是广场还是人群，主体都处在一个包围他的整体之中。

intro.en: Midst is a short native noun built on the Old English middle stem, with amid and amidst as close relatives.
intro.cn: midst 是本土短名词，建立在古英语「中间」词干之上，amid 与 amidst 是它的近亲。

latinIntro.en: Midst has no Latin ancestor, but it can be compared with Latin medius, the source of mediate and medium.
latinIntro.cn: midst 没有拉丁语祖先，不过可以与拉丁语 medius（中间的）对照，后者是 mediate、medium 的来源。

items.example: Middle shares the stem of midst.
items.exampleCN: middle 与 midst 共享词干。

items.example: Amid came from an old phrase for in the middle.
items.exampleCN: amid 源自古代表「在中间」的短语。

items.example: Amidst adds the same place ending as midst.
items.exampleCN: amidst 与 midst 带有同样的地点词尾。

items.example: The prefix mid appears in midday and midnight.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mid 出现在 midday 与 midnight 中。

items.example: Median is a Latin cousin of midst.
items.exampleCN: median 是 midst 的拉丁语远亲。

items.example: Mediate keeps the idea of standing between sides.
items.exampleCN: mediate 保留了「站在双方中间」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 与地点或状态有关的古老词尾
items.example: The ending in midst marks a place, not a comparison.
items.exampleCN: midst 的词尾表示地点，而非比较级。

items.example: The place ending also appears in amidst.
items.exampleCN: 这一表地点的词尾也出现在 amidst 中。

definition_zh: 强大的；巨大的；非常重要的
definition_en: very powerful, very large, or very important
core_image: 一只巨大的拳头举起，影子压过整片山谷
scene: 暴雨连着下了三天，河水漫过堤岸，冲走了整片村庄。The mighty river swept away the whole village after three days of rain.
sceneCN: 这里 mighty 是「强大的、威猛的」（第 1 个义项：力量或势力极其强大）；句意：这条威力强大的河流在大雨三天后冲走了整个村庄。

pos.zh: 强大的；有权势的；巨大的
非常；极其（多用于口语加强语气）

collocations.zh: 非常震撼的；非常令人印象深刻

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，去掉 -y 后的词干，义为「力量；威力」
mighty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「极大地；猛烈地」
mighty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「强大；威力」
all（全部）+ mighty（强大）构成，义为「全能的；无所不能的」

senses.title: Having great power
senses.definition: having or showing very great power, strength, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或显示出极大的力量、体力或权威
senses.example: The mighty army marched toward the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那支强大的军队向边境开进。
senses.why: The root might means strength or power, so the first sense describes whatever holds overwhelming force.
senses.whyCN: 词根 might 表示「力量、威力」，所以这个词最先形容拥有压倒性力量的事物。

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: very large, loud, or impressive in size or scale
senses.definitionCN: 体积、规模或声势极大、给人以震撼
senses.example: A mighty wave crashed over the seawall.
senses.exampleCN: 一个巨浪砸过防波堤。
senses.why: Something with great power usually looks huge, so the word naturally extends from strength to sheer size.
senses.whyCN: 力量大的东西往往看起来也巨大，于是这个词从「强」自然扩展到「大」。

senses.title: Very important and significant
senses.definition: very serious or important in its consequences
senses.definitionCN: 后果非常重大、影响深远的
senses.example: Treaty talks were a mighty step toward peace.
senses.exampleCN: 条约谈判是迈向和平的重大一步。
senses.why: Power that shapes events becomes importance, so a mighty step means a step that changes everything.
senses.whyCN: 能左右事件走向的力量就变成了「重要性」，所以 mighty step 指改变全局的一步。

senses.title: Very, as an intensifier
senses.definition: used informally before an adjective to mean very
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在形容词前，表示「非常、极其」
senses.example: That was a mighty fine dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 那顿晚饭真是好极了。
senses.why: The spoken sense turns raw power into feeling, letting the word simply push any adjective to the extreme.
senses.whyCN: 口语义把「力量」转化为「感受」，让这个词只是把形容词推向极端。

senses.title: High and arrogant, in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: acting as if more important than other people, in high and mighty
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 high and mighty 中表示自以为高人一等、态度傲慢
senses.example: The new manager acts high and mighty with her staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理对下属摆出一副高高在上的样子。
senses.why: The phrase high and mighty stacks height and power together, so the sense turns into looking down on others.
senses.whyCN: 短语 high and mighty 把「高」和「强」叠在一起，于是衍生出俯视别人的傲慢义。

intro.en: Mighty is built on might, which comes from Old English miht, related to the verb magan, meaning to be able.
intro.cn: mighty 由 might 构成，后者来自古英语 miht，与动词 magan（能够）相关。

items.en: A reconstructed form magin means power or ability.
items.cn: 重构形式 magin 表示「力量、能力」。

items.en: Miht means power, strength, or ability.
items.cn: 古英语 miht 表示力量、威力或能力。

items.en: Mihtig already means powerful, adding the ending -ig.
items.cn: 古英语 mihtig 已表示「强大的」，由词尾 -ig 构成。

items.en: The spelling shifts to mighti and mighty.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 mighti，再变为 mighty。

items.en: The word is used for rivers and storms as well as rulers.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词用于河流与风暴，而不只是统治者。

items.en: The informal adverb sense is common in speech.
items.cn: 口语中常用的副词义在二十世纪广泛流行。

note.en: Mighty shares the root might with almighty and mightily, and stands near words for strength.
note.cn: mighty 与 almighty、mightily 共享 might 词根，并与表示「力量」的词语意义相邻。

entries.definition: great power
entries.definitionCN: 同源，义为「力量；威力」，也是情态动词，此处两类含义易混

entries.definition: to a great degree
entries.definitionCN: mighty 加 -ly 的副词，义为「极大地；猛烈地」

entries.definition: having complete power
entries.definitionCN: all + mighty 复合词，义为「全能的」

entries.definition: able to control people or events
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「强大的；有势力的」

entries.definition: having great physical force
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「强壮的；牢固的」

entries.definition: extremely large
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「巨大的」，偏重体积而非力量

normalIntro.en: Mighty is might plus -y: the noun for power turned into an adjective for powerful things.
normalIntro.cn: mighty 就是 might 加 -y：把表示「力量」的名词变成形容「强大」的形容词。

normal.en: Forget the root might and just remember that mighty comes from it.
normal.cn: 记住词根 might 表示力量，mighty 由它加上 -y 而来。

normal.en: In high and mighty the phrase usually criticises someone who looks down on others.
normal.cn: high and mighty 通常带贬义，批评看不起别人的人。

normal.en: Rivers, waves, and storms are often called mighty in writing.
normal.cn: 在书面语里，河流、巨浪、风暴常被称作 mighty。

normal.en: The adverb mighty before an adjective means very, as in mighty good.
normal.cn: 副词 mighty 放在形容词前表示「非常」，如 mighty good。

normal.en: Compare powerful and strong: powerful is political, strong is physical, mighty covers both plus a literary tone.
normal.cn: 对比 powerful 与 strong：前者偏政治，后者偏体力，mighty 兼指两者并带文学色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a giant fist casting a shadow over a whole valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一只巨大的拳头把影子投满整条山谷。

abstract.en: See an old castle gate opening under a crown carved in stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇古老的城堡大门在石刻王冠下打开。

abstract.en: Imagine a river so wide that a bridge looks like a thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条大河宽到桥看起来只是一条细线。

examples.en: The mighty walls of the city have stood for a thousand years.
examples.cn: 这座城市的雄伟城墙已经矗立了一千年。

examples.en: She made a mighty effort to finish the marathon.
examples.cn: 她拼尽全力跑完了马拉松。

examples.en: He was once a mighty king, but now he lives quietly.
examples.cn: 他曾是一位强大的国王，如今却过着平静的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埋」得深的「铁」——一铁块沉在地底，谁也搬不动，象征力量巨大；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语 magin（力量、能力）→ 古英语 miht（力量）+ -ig（具有……的）→ mihtig → 中古英语 mighti → 英语 mighty，核心义「拥有压倒性力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Mighty begins with raw power, widens to enormous size, then to importance, and finally turns into an everyday intensifier and an idiom for arrogance.
sensesIntro.cn: mighty 先指原始的力量，再扩展到巨大的规模，进而表示重要性，最后变成日常口语的加强词和表示傲慢的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a huge fist raised, its shadow covering the whole valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只巨拳高高举起，影子罩住整条山谷。

branches.en: Great power is the direct outcome of the core image.
branches.cn: 强大的力量是核心意象最直接的延伸。

branches.en: Great size grows out of power because big things carry force.
branches.cn: 「巨大」源自「有力」，因为庞然大物本身就有威力。

branches.en: Importance is power that changes the course of events.
branches.cn: 重大性就是能改变事件走向的力量。

branches.en: The spoken intensifier stretches power into a general degree word.
branches.cn: 口语加强词把力量延伸为一个表示程度的泛用词。

branches.en: The idiom high and mighty turns power into social arrogance.
branches.cn: 习语 high and mighty 把力量转成了社会意义上的傲慢。

intro.en: Mighty is might plus the adjective ending -y, with -ly and -ness forms built on top.
intro.cn: mighty 由 might 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，再派生出 -ly 与 -ness 形式。

latinIntro.en: Mighty is a Germanic word with no Latin source, though Latin potens and magnus describe similar ideas.
latinIntro.cn: mighty 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语来源，不过拉丁语 potens 与 magnus 表达了相近的意思。

items.example: Magan is the old verb behind might.
items.exampleCN: magan 是 might 背后的古老动词。

items.example: Miht is the direct noun ancestor.
items.exampleCN: miht 是直接的名词祖先。

items.example: Might is the base that mighty grows from.
items.exampleCN: might 是 mighty 生长出来的基础。

items.example: The suffix -y turns might into mighty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 might 变成 mighty。

items.example: The old ending -ig produced mihtig.
items.exampleCN: 古词尾 -ig 构成了 mihtig。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mightily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mightily。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms mightiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 mightiness。

items.example: The prefix all- forms almighty.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 all- 构成 almighty。

definition_zh: 移民；移居者；候鸟
definition_en: a person or animal that moves from one place to another to live or work
core_image: 拎着行李箱赶车的人，身后是渐渐远去的家
scene: 清晨的车站里，一位母亲抱着孩子提着箱子，赶去另一座城市找工作。A young migrant left the village station in search of work in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 migrant 是「移居者、打工移民」（第 1 个义项：为生活或工作迁居到别处的人）；句意：这位年轻的移居者离开乡村车站，去城市找工作。

pos.zh: 移民；移居者；候鸟；迁徙动物

collocations.zh: 经济移民（为生计而迁移的人）

derivatives.zh: 无前缀的动词形式，义为「迁移；移居」，构词分析中的自由词根
migrate 加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「迁移；移居」
migrate 加 -ory 构成的形容词，义为「迁徙的；流动的」
前缀 im-（向内）+ migrant 构成，义为「入境移民」
前缀 e-（向外）+ migrant 构成，义为「出境移民」

senses.title: A person who moves to live or work
senses.definition: a person who moves from one country or region to another to live or work
senses.definitionCN: 从一国或一地迁到另一国或另一地居住或工作的人
senses.example: Many migrants send money home every month.
senses.exampleCN: 许多移民每月给家里寄钱。
senses.why: The Latin verb migrare means to move to another place, and migrant names the person who does the moving.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 migrare 意为「迁往他处」，migrant 即指那个进行迁移的人。

senses.title: A moving animal or bird
senses.definition: an animal or bird that travels to another region with the seasons
senses.definitionCN: 随季节迁往另一地区的鸟或动物
senses.example: The lakes attract migrants every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天这些湖泊都会引来候鸟。
senses.why: Animals that follow the seasons behave exactly like human movers, so the same word covers them without change.
senses.whyCN: 随季节迁徙的动物与人类迁居者的行为结构相同，因此同一个词不必改动就能指它们。

senses.title: The adjective for travel and movement
senses.definition: describing people, groups, or routes that involve regular movement
senses.definitionCN: 形容涉及经常性迁徙的人、群体或路线
senses.example: The factory relies on a migrant workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂依靠流动的劳动力。
senses.why: The noun was reused as a modifier, so migrant worker and migrant labour simply mean a worker or labour force on the move.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词被借作修饰语，于是 migrant worker 与 migrant labour 就是「在流动的工人或劳动力」。

senses.title: A seasonal or temporary traveller
senses.definition: a person who moves for part of the year to do seasonal work
senses.definitionCN: 每年只在一段时间内为了做季节性工作而迁移的人
senses.example: The farm hires migrants to pick fruit each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场每年夏天雇人来摘水果。
senses.why: Because the move does not have to be permanent, migrant can also mean a seasonal traveller who returns home afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 因为迁移不一定永久，migrant 也可以指季节性出来干活、之后又回家的人。

senses.title: A person or group that shifts in effect
senses.definition: in wider use, a person or group that regularly moves from one place, job, or attachment to another
senses.definitionCN: 更宽泛地指经常在各地、各工作之间转移的人或群体
senses.example: As a migrant between jobs, he learned every trade quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 作为频繁换工作的人，他很快学会了每一门手艺。
senses.why: Once the word means moving, it loosens from geography and can describe anyone who keeps changing position.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「移动」，就脱离了纯地理含义，也可形容不断更换位置的人。

intro.en: Migrant comes from Latin migrare, to move from one place to another, and names the one who moves.
intro.cn: migrant 来自拉丁语 migrare（从一处迁往另一处），指进行迁移的那一方。

items.en: Migrare means to move, change place, or migrate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 意为移动、换地方、迁移。

items.en: Migrans is its present participle, the migrating one.
items.cn: migrans 是它的现在分词，意为「正在迁移的」。

items.en: Migrare passes through scholarly Latin into English.
items.cn: migrare 经学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun migrant appears as an English word for a moving person or animal.
items.cn: 英语 migrant 作为名词出现，指迁移中的人或动物。

items.en: The word becomes common in migration law, labour, and wildlife studies.
items.cn: 现代英语中它常见于移民法、劳动力与野生动物研究中。

note.en: Migrant shares the migrate root with immigration words, and sits beside words for people who leave and arrive.
note.cn: migrant 与 immi-、emi- 类词共享 migrate 词根，并与表示「离开」和「抵达」的人群词相邻。

entries.definition: to move to another place
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「迁移；移居」

entries.definition: the act of moving
entries.definitionCN: 由同源动词加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「迁移；移居」

entries.definition: moving with the seasons
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「迁徙的」，形式与 migrant 很接近

entries.definition: a person who comes to a country
entries.definitionCN: im- 前缀指向内 + migrant，义为「入境移民」，拼写极易与 migrant 混

entries.definition: a person who leaves a country
entries.definitionCN: 近义，e- 前缀指向外，义为「出境移民」

entries.definition: a person who goes to live in a new place
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「定居者」，强调在新地扎根

entries.definition: a person forced to flee danger
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「难民」，强调被迫逃离，而非自主迁移

normalIntro.en: Migrant is migrare plus the -ant ending, the one who is moving.
normalIntro.cn: migrant 就是 migrare 加词尾 -ant，指「正在迁移的那个」。

normal.en: The suffix -ant marks a person, just as it does in assistant.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ant 表示「做某事的人」，正如 assistant 中的用法。

normal.en: Mix up immigrant and emigrant and you will remember the prefixes in and out.
normal.cn: 把 immigrant 与 emigrant 放在一起记，就记住了「向内」与「向外」两个前缀。

normal.en: Birders call seasonal travellers migrants, which links birds with people.
normal.cn: 观鸟者把季节迁徙的鸟也叫 migrants，这就把鸟与人连在一起。

normal.en: Migrant labour usually suggests work, while migration may simply be about moving home.
normal.cn: migrant labour 往往暗含「打工」，而 migration 可以只是搬家。

normal.en: Compare refugee: a refugee is forced to flee, a migrant chooses or needs to move.
normal.cn: 对比 refugee：难民是被迫逃离，移居者则是主动或出于生计而迁移。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase with a home address still taped to the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱，把手上还贴着旧家的地址。

abstract.en: See a flock of geese flying north in a long arrow overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象头顶一群大雁排成箭头向北飞去。

abstract.en: Imagine a farm truck in summer carrying people from far away to pick fruit.
abstract.cn: 想象夏天一辆农场卡车载着远道而来的人去摘水果。

examples.en: Many migrants work in the city and send money to their villages.
examples.cn: 许多移居者在城市打工，再把钱寄回村子。

examples.en: The migrant birds return to the same wetland every winter.
examples.cn: 这些候鸟每年冬天都回到同一片湿地。

examples.en: The government is reviewing its policy on migrant workers.
examples.cn: 政府正在审议其外来务工者政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖个软的」——行李太软不好搬，只好一路往别处走，就成了 migrant；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 migrare（迁往他处）→ 现在分词 migrans → 英语名词 migrant（迁移中的人或动物），核心义「离开原地、前往他方」。

sensesIntro.en: Migrant starts with the human mover, spreads to birds and other animals, then to the adjective use, seasonal travellers, and looser cases of changing position.
sensesIntro.cn: migrant 先指迁移的人，再扩展到鸟和其他动物，然后用作形容词，接着指季节性流动者，最后泛指不断更换位置的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller with a suitcase moving away from a familiar home.
core.cn: 核心意象：拎着行李箱的人，正离开熟悉的家。

branches.en: The human mover is the central and most frequent branch.
branches.cn: 迁移的人是最核心、最常用的分支。

branches.en: Seasonal birds and animals share the same act of moving.
branches.cn: 随季节迁徙的鸟兽共享同一种迁移行为。

branches.en: The modifier use describes groups or routes built on movement.
branches.cn: 修饰语用法描述建立在流动之上的群体或路线。

branches.en: Seasonal work gives a branch for travellers who return home.
branches.cn: 季节性工作延伸出「出来干活、之后回家」这一类流动者。

branches.en: Both branches loosen geography into the general idea of switching jobs or places.
branches.cn: 这两个分支都把地理意义放宽，变成「换工作、换地方」的一般概念。

intro.en: Migrant is the Latin root migrare with the participant ending -ant, and it forms a large family with im- and e- prefixes.
intro.cn: migrant 由拉丁词根 migrare 加表示行为者的词尾 -ant 构成，并与 im-、e- 前缀构成一个大家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare means to move or change place, and migrans is its present participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 意为移动或换地方，migrans 是它的现在分词。

items.example: The root migr- serves as the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 migr- 是整个词族的核心。

items.example: Migrare is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: migrare 是直接的动词来源。

items.example: Migrans shapes the ending of migrant.
items.exampleCN: migrans 决定了 migrant 的词尾。

items.meaning: the person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -ant forms a noun of the doer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成表示行为者的名词。

items.example: Migrate is the simple English verb.
items.exampleCN: migrate 是简单的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms migration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 migration。

items.example: The prefix im- forms immigrant.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 immigrant。

items.example: The prefix e- forms emigrant.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 构成 emigrant。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms migratory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 migratory。

definition_zh: 里程碑；重要转折点；路程石标；整数寿辰
definition_en: an important event or point in a process, or a stone marking a distance on a road
core_image: 路边一块刻着里数的石头，标出已经走过的距离
scene: 项目进行到一半，团队终于交付了第一个可用版本，大家把这天写进日程表，称作重要的里程碑——从那天起，余下的工作都有了参照。The team called the launch of the first working version a major milestone.
sceneCN: 这里 milestone 是「里程碑、重要转折点」（第 1 个义项：进程中的关键事件）；句意：团队把第一个可用版本的发布称作一个重要的里程碑。

pos.zh: 里程碑；重要转折点；里程碑式事件

derivatives.zh: 以里程碑为节点的，多见于项目管理语境
英里，构成 milestone 的前半，拉丁语「千步」之意
里程；英里数，以 -age 后缀构成

senses.title: A key moment in a process
senses.definition: an important event or stage that marks real progress in a process
senses.definitionCN: 标志进展的重要事件或阶段
senses.example: Finishing the trial was a milestone for the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 完成试验是研究团队的一个里程碑。
senses.why: The road stone once told travellers how far they had come; the same image now marks how far a project has advanced.
senses.whyCN: 路边的石标原本告诉行人走了多远，如今这张画面转用来标记一项工程推进到了哪一步。

senses.title: A stone by the road
senses.definition: a stone placed beside a road to show the distance to a town
senses.definitionCN: 设在路旁、标明到某地距离的石标
senses.example: An old milestone still stands beside the Roman road.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马古道旁仍立着一块古老的里程石标。
senses.why: The compound literally joins mile and stone, so the first meaning is simply the marked rock on the road.
senses.whyCN: 这个合成词字面上就是「英里」加「石头」，因此最本初的含义就是路边那块作标记的石头。

senses.title: A way to measure
senses.definition: something used as a standard for judging how far a person or plan has got
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断某人或某计划进展程度的标准
senses.example: Test scores are only one milestone of progress.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩只是衡量进步的一种尺度。
senses.why: Because the stone numbers distances, it also works as a scale for judging how far anything has travelled.
senses.whyCN: 正因为石标为距离编号，它也成了判断任何事物走了多远的刻度。

senses.title: An age worth marking
senses.definition: a birthday with a round number aged, often the fortieth or sixtieth
senses.definitionCN: 年龄为整数的生日，常指四十岁或六十岁
senses.example: Her sixtieth birthday was a family milestone.
senses.exampleCN: 她的六十岁生日是全家的一件大事。
senses.why: A round age stands on the time line like a stone on the road, so people stop and mark it.
senses.whyCN: 整数年龄像路上的一块石标立在人生时间线上，人们因此会停下脚步做记号。

intro.en: Milestone joins mile, a distance from Latin mille passus, and the English noun stone.
intro.cn: milestone 由 mile（英里，源出拉丁语 mille passus「千步」）与英语名词 stone（石头）组合而成。

items.en: Mille passus means a thousand paces, the Roman unit of a mile.
items.cn: mille passus 意为「千步」，是罗马人的一英里单位。

items.en: Mil becomes the English measure word for a long distance.
items.cn: mil 成为英语中表示长距离的量词。

items.en: Stan means stone, and stands for the marker itself.
items.cn: stan 意为石头，代表标石本身。

items.en: Milestone names the stone set along a road to record distance.
items.cn: milestone 指沿路安置、记录里程的石标。

items.en: The stone sense widens into any important stage or turning point.
items.cn: 从「石标」扩展为任何重要的阶段或转折点。

note.en: Milestone is a compound of mile and stone, close to other distance stones and to words for turning points.
note.cn: milestone 是 mile 与 stone 构成的合成词，与各类路标石，以及表示转折的词语相邻。

entries.definition: a unit of distance equal to about one and a half kilometres
entries.definitionCN: 英里，约合一点六公里的距离单位

entries.definition: the distance travelled measured in miles
a post that shows the distance along a road
entries.definitionCN: 路旁的里数标志柱，与 milestone 几乎同义

entries.definition: a moment when a process changes direction
a visible object or event that marks a stage
entries.definitionCN: 地标；具有标志意义的事件

entries.definition: a sudden important advance

normalIntro.en: Milestone is literally a mile stone: a marker that says how far you have come.
normalIntro.cn: milestone 字面上就是「英里石」：一块标出你已走了多远的记号石头。

normal.en: Mile comes from Latin for a thousand paces.
normal.cn: mile 源于拉丁语「千步」的说法。

normal.en: Stone is the English word for the marker rock itself.
normal.cn: stone 就是英语里表示「石头」的词，指那块标石。

normal.en: Notice that the two halves of the word are both still visible.
normal.cn: 注意这个词的两个部分如今仍清晰可辨：英里加石头。

normal.en: Reach a milestone means to arrive at an important stage.
normal.cn: reach a milestone 表示抵达一个重要阶段。

normal.en: Compare landmark: landmark marks a place, milestone marks a stage.
normal.cn: 对比 landmark：landmark 标记地点，milestone 标记阶段。

abstract.en: See a line of stones along a road, each with a number carved on it.
abstract.cn: 想象路边一排石头，每块上都刻着数字。

abstract.en: Think of a hiker who stops beside one stone and smiles at how far she has come.
abstract.cn: 想象一位徒步者在石标旁停下，为走过的路程露出微笑。

abstract.en: Think of a scale in a laboratory, used to weigh how much progress a study has made.
abstract.cn: 想象实验室里的一台秤，用来称量研究推进了多少。

examples.en: Becoming a parent is a major milestone in many lives.
examples.cn: 为人父母是许多人人生中的重大里程碑。

examples.en: The bridge was an engineering milestone of its age.
examples.cn: 这座桥是它那个时代的工程里程碑。

examples.en: Surviving the winter was the first milestone on the journey north.
examples.cn: 熬过冬天是北行旅途上的第一块里程碑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈而走」——每迈过一段路就立一块石头做记号；这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 mile（英里，源自拉丁语 mille passus「千步」）+ stone（石头）→ 路边标明距离的石标 → 引申为「进程中的重要节点」。

sensesIntro.en: Milestone begins as a road stone, turns into a measure of progress, then a key stage, and finally a landmark age.
sensesIntro.cn: milestone 先从路边的石标起步，转为衡量进度的尺度，再指关键阶段，最后用于整数寿辰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved stone beside the road, marking the distance travelled.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边一块刻着里数的石头，标出已经走过的距离。

branches.en: A key moment in a process is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 进程中的关键时刻是现代主导义项。

branches.en: The stone beside the road keeps the original meaning.
branches.cn: 路边的石标保留了最初的实体含义。

branches.en: Using a stone to judge progress gives the measuring sense.
branches.cn: 用石标来判断进展，就有了衡量尺度的含义。

branches.en: A round age sits on the time line like a stone on the road.
branches.cn: 整数年龄像路上的石标一样落在时间线上。

branches.en: A marked stage and a way of measuring progress are two sides of one idea.
branches.cn: 被标记的阶段与衡量进展的方式是同一想法的两面。

intro.en: Milestone is an English compound of mile and stone, with no Latin suffix of its own.
intro.cn: milestone 是 mile 与 stone 组成的英语合成词，本身没有拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind mile is mille passus, a thousand paces.
latinIntro.cn: mile 背后的拉丁语是 mille passus，即「千步」。

items.example: Mile supplies the distance idea.
items.exampleCN: mile 提供距离的概念。

items.example: Mille is the Latin word for a thousand.
items.exampleCN: mille 是拉丁语的「一千」。

items.example: Stone is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: stone 是合成词的后半部分。

items.example: The element -stone forms many marker nouns.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -stone 构成许多标记类名词。

items.example: Milepost is a near twin of milestone.
items.exampleCN: milepost 与 milestone 几乎是同义词。

items.meaning: a marker of distance or progress
items.example: Milestone keeps both the stone and stage senses.
items.exampleCN: milestone 同时保留石标与阶段两种含义。

items.example: The suffix -age builds mileage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 mileage。

items.example: Project plans are often milestone-based.
items.exampleCN: 项目计划常以里程碑为节点。

latinEntries.example: Mille is the core of mile.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mille 是 mile 的核心。

latinEntries.example: Milia passuum lies behind the modern mile.
latinEntries.exampleCN: milia passuum 是现代 mile 的来源。

definition_zh: 激进的；好战的；好斗的；激进分子
definition_en: ready to use strong or even violent action to support a cause, or a person who does this
core_image: 一个人把拳头攥紧举过头顶，随时准备冲突
scene: 在游行队伍最前面，有人高举标语、大声喊话，警方也被请来维持秩序——这样的行动者常被称为激进分子。The group is known for its militant members, who take action at any cost.
sceneCN: 这里 militant 是「激进的、好战的」（第 1 个义项：随时准备以强硬手段达成目标的）；句意：这个团体以其激进的成员闻名，他们不惜代价采取行动。

derivatives.zh: 激进；好斗作风，名词后缀 -ancy 由形容词构成
激进地；好斗地，副词后缀 -ly
军国主义，与 militant 同出拉丁语 miles（士兵）

senses.title: Ready to fight for a cause
senses.definition: willing to use strong, sometimes violent means to promote a political or social cause
senses.definitionCN: 愿意用强硬甚至暴力手段推动政治或社会目标的
senses.example: Militant unions staged a wave of strikes last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 激进的工会去年春天发动了一波罢工。
senses.why: The Latin root miles means a soldier, so the word carries the image of a cause defended as if on a battlefield.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 miles 意为「士兵」，所以这个词自带一种像在战场上捍卫某项事业的画面。

senses.title: Aggressive in bearing
senses.definition: showing a fierce and combative attitude toward others in everyday dealings
senses.definitionCN: 在日常交往中表现出凶悍、好斗态度的
senses.example: His militant manner made negotiation almost impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 他咄咄逼人的态度几乎让谈判无法进行。
senses.why: Once the soldier image is applied to everyday behaviour, it describes anyone who meets others like an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 当「士兵」的形象被用到日常行为上，它就可以形容任何把他人当对手来对待的人。

senses.title: A person who fights
senses.definition: a person who takes strong or violent action for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 为某项事业采取强硬甚至暴力行动的人
senses.example: Several militants were arrested after the protest.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议之后，几名激进分子被逮捕。
senses.why: English turns many adjectives into nouns, so the one ready to fight becomes the fighter himself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接当名词用，于是「准备战斗的人」就成了「战斗者本人」。

intro.en: Militant comes from Latin miles, a soldier, through the verb militare, to serve as a soldier.
intro.cn: militant 来自拉丁语 miles（士兵），经由动词 militare（服兵役）而来。

items.en: Miles is the Latin word for a soldier.
items.cn: miles 是拉丁语中「士兵」的说法。

items.en: Militare means to serve as a soldier, and carries the sense of active service.
items.cn: militare 意为服兵役，带有「积极效力」的意味。

items.en: Militans is the present participle, one who is serving or fighting.
items.cn: militans 是现在分词，指正在服役或作战的人。

items.en: Militant passes into French with the sense of warfare.
items.cn: militant 进入法语，带上了战争、争斗的意思。

items.en: English first uses militant for fighting or warlike things.
items.cn: 英语最初用 militant 形容与战斗、战争有关的。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word mostly describes aggressive campaigners for a cause.
items.cn: 十九世纪之后，该词主要形容为某项事业咄咄逼人地奔走的人。

note.en: Militant shares its root with a whole soldier family in English, and sits close to words for radicals and fighters.
note.cn: militant 在英语中与一整套表示「士兵」的词同根，并与表示激进派、斗士的词相邻。

entries.definition: connected with soldiers or armed forces
a fighting force of ordinary citizens
the belief that a country should build strong armed forces
favouring extreme political change
entries.definitionCN: 激进的；主张彻底变革的

entries.definition: a determined campaigner for a cause
a person with extreme enthusiasm for a belief

normalIntro.en: Militant carries the Latin soldier miles inside it, so it always smells of battle.
normalIntro.cn: militant 内部藏着拉丁语「士兵」miles，所以它总带着战场的气息。

normal.en: Miles means soldier in Latin, and militant means acting like one.
normal.cn: miles 在拉丁语里是士兵，militant 就是「像士兵一样行事」。

normal.en: Military and militia share the same stem.
normal.cn: military 与 militia 共用同一个词干。

normal.en: The noun suffix -ancy turns it into militancy.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -ancy 把它变成 militancy。

normal.en: A militant group is not merely angry but ready to act.
normal.cn: militant group 不只是生气，而是准备行动。

normal.en: Compare military: military describes armies, militant describes people who act like soldiers for a cause.
normal.cn: 对比 military：military 描述军队，militant 描述为某项事业像士兵那样行动的人。

abstract.en: Picture a raised fist above a crowd, held still and ready.
abstract.cn: 想象人群中一只高举的拳头，纹丝不动，随时准备挥出。

abstract.en: Picture a person leaning forward over a table, fists on the wood, arguing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人前倾伏在桌面上，双拳抵着木头，激烈争辩。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier who has put down the rifle but kept the uniform.
abstract.cn: 想象一名士兵放下步枪，却仍穿着那身军装。

examples.en: The government accused the militant wing of planning the attack.
examples.cn: 政府指控该组织的激进派策划了袭击。

examples.en: She became more militant after her letters went unanswered.
examples.cn: 信件无人回复之后，她变得更加激进。

examples.en: Two militants were arrested at the border.
examples.cn: 两名激进分子在边境被捕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米里坦」——米袋里藏着一根棍棒，随时能抄起来，像好斗的士兵；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 miles（士兵）+ 动词 militare（服兵役）→ 现在分词 militans → 法语 militant → 英语 militant，核心是「像士兵一样为某事作战」。

sensesIntro.en: Militant starts from the soldier image, moves to aggressive daily behaviour, and then to the person who acts that way.
sensesIntro.cn: militant 从「士兵」的形象出发，先指为事业强硬作战，再指日常的咄咄逼人，最后指这样行事的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised fist, held ready above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中一只高举、随时可以挥出的拳头。

branches.en: Fighting for a cause is the main political adjective sense.
branches.cn: 为事业而战是主要的政治形容词义项。

branches.en: Extending the soldier image to daily conduct gives the aggressive sense.
branches.cn: 把士兵形象延伸到日常行为，就有了咄咄逼人的义项。

branches.en: The adjective turns into the person who takes the action.
branches.cn: 形容词转化为采取行动的人，即名词义项。

branches.en: A fierce stance on politics and a fierce manner at table share one temper.
branches.cn: 政治上的强硬立场与谈话时的强硬态度共享同一种脾气。

branches.en: The adjective describes the cause and the noun names the fighter.
branches.cn: 形容词语义指向事业，名词语义指向斗争者本人。

intro.en: Militant comes from the Latin soldier root miles, and the suffix -ant makes it an adjective or a person noun.
intro.cn: militant 来自拉丁语「士兵」词根 miles，后缀 -ant 使它成为形容词或指人的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin miles means soldier, and militare means to serve as a soldier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 miles 意为士兵，militare 意为服兵役。

items.example: Miles is the heart of the whole word family.
items.exampleCN: miles 是整个词族的核心。

items.example: Militare gives the sense of active service.
items.exampleCN: militare 提供「积极服役」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态或做某事的
items.example: The suffix -ant forms militant from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 由动词词干构成 militant。

items.example: The suffix -ancy forms militancy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ancy 构成 militancy。

items.example: Military is the most common sibling.
items.exampleCN: military 是最常用的同族词。

items.example: Militia keeps the soldier sense in a civilian form.
items.exampleCN: militia 以平民形式保留「士兵」含义。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms militarise.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 构成 militarise。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb militantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 militantly。

definition_zh: 千年期；千禧年；一千年；黄金时代
definition_en: a period of one thousand years, or the turning point when such a period begins
core_image: 一条时间线上被刻出一千个格子的长段，尽头处亮起一道道标线
scene: 跨年夜，城市广场挤满人群，倒数结束的那一刻钟声齐鸣，大家都在谈论新千年的开端。Crowds gathered in the square to welcome the new millennium.
sceneCN: 这里 millennium 是「千年期」（第 1 个义项：一千年的一段时间）；句意：人群聚集在广场上迎接新千年。

derivatives.zh: 千年的；千年之交的，后缀 -ial 由名词构成形容词
千禧一代，常作复数 millennials
存在了一千年的，由名词加形容词构成复合词

senses.title: A thousand years
senses.definition: a period of one thousand years
senses.definitionCN: 长度为整整一千年的时期
senses.example: The temple has stood for well over a millennium.
senses.exampleCN: 这座神庙已经矗立了远超一千年。
senses.why: Latin mille means a thousand and annus means year, so the word simply counts out a thousand years in one breath.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mille 意为「一千」，annus 意为「年」，这个词就是把一千年一口气数成了一个整体。

senses.title: The year one thousand
senses.definition: the point in time when a thousand-year period ends and the next begins, especially the year two thousand
senses.definitionCN: 某个千年结束、下一个千年开始的时刻，尤指二〇〇〇年
senses.example: People feared computers would fail at the millennium.
senses.exampleCN: 人们担心计算机会在千禧年之交出故障。
senses.why: A marked thousandth year turns the count itself into a party, so the word also names the moment of arrival.
senses.whyCN: 第一千个年头一到，数数本身就成了庆典，于是这个词也指名到达的那一刻。

senses.title: A hoped-for golden age
senses.definition: a period of peace and perfect happiness, especially one expected in the future
senses.definitionCN: 和平又圆满、尤其指人们对未来所期待的时期
senses.example: The preacher promised a millennium of justice and peace.
senses.exampleCN: 传道者许诺了一个充满公义与和平的黄金时代。
senses.why: Religious writing said Christ would reign for a thousand years, so the thousand-year span came to mean paradise on earth.
senses.whyCN: 宗教文献说基督将统治一千年，于是「千年」这段时光逐渐有了人间天国的含义。

intro.en: Millennium is Latin mille, a thousand, plus annus, a year, built together in the early modern period.
intro.cn: millennium 由拉丁语 mille（一千）与 annus（年）组合而成，形成于近代早期。

items.en: Mille means a thousand.
items.cn: mille 意为「一千」。

items.en: Annus means a year, and survives in annual, annals, and anniversary.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，其身影保留在 annual、annals 与 anniversary 中。

items.en: Millennium is formed as a Latin compound of a thousand and a year.
items.cn: millennium 作为拉丁语合成词，由「一千」与「年」构成。

items.en: Millennium enters English through learned Latin church writing.
items.cn: millennium 经由教会学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: English extends the word from a biblical thousand-year reign to any thousand-year span or its turning point.
items.cn: 英语把该词从《圣经》中的千年统治，扩展到任何一千年的时段及其转折时刻。

note.en: Millennium shares the Latin thousand with the mile, and sits near other long periods and near golden-age language.
note.cn: millennium 与 mile 共享拉丁语的「一千」，并与各种长时段词及「黄金时代」类说法相邻。

entries.definition: lasting or turning a thousand years
entries.definitionCN: 持续千年的；千年之交的

entries.definition: the Latin word for a thousand
happening once every year
a period of one hundred years
a period of ten years
a period of great happiness or success
entries.definitionCN: 黄金时代，极兴旺幸福的时期

normalIntro.en: Millennium hides a thousand and a year inside it: mille plus annus.
normalIntro.cn: millennium 里面藏着一个「一千」和「一年」：mille 加 annus。

normal.en: Mille is Latin for a thousand, as in millimeter or mile.
normal.cn: mille 是拉丁语的「一千」，如 millimeter 和 mile 都含此意。

normal.en: Annus is Latin for a year, as in annual and anniversary.
normal.cn: annus 是拉丁语的「年」，如 annual 和 anniversary。

normal.en: Put them together and you get a thousand years.
normal.cn: 把两者合在一起，得到的就是一千年。

normal.en: The Latin plural is millennia, and millennia is much more common than millenniums.
normal.cn: 拉丁语复数形式 millennia 比英语化的 millenniums 常用得多。

normal.en: Compare century: a century is born from centum, hundred, and a millennium from mille, thousand.
normal.cn: 对比 century：世纪来自 centum（一百），千年来自 mille（一千）。

abstract.en: See a very long ruler with a thousand marks, lit only at the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻着一千格的极长的尺子，只有最后一格亮着灯。

abstract.en: Picture a clock tower at midnight, bells ringing as crowds count down.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜的钟楼，人群倒数时钟声齐鸣。

abstract.en: Picture a garden gate opening onto a land of endless peace.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇花园门打开，门后是一片永远安宁的土地。

examples.en: The written record covers more than two millennia.
examples.cn: 文字记录跨越了两千多年。

examples.en: The city plans to finish the railway before the next millennium begins.
examples.cn: 这座城市计划在下一个千年到来之前建成这条铁路。

examples.en: Some followers expected a millennium of peace within their lifetime.
examples.cn: 一些追随者期待在有生之年见到一个千年黄金时代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米莲年」——一池米里生出一千朵莲，每朵代表一年；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mille（一千）+ annus（年）→ millennium（一千年）→ 千禧年、千年的开端，再引申为理想的黄金时代。

sensesIntro.en: Millennium counts out a thousand years, names the moment they turn over, and then, through religious writing, means a hoped-for golden age.
sensesIntro.cn: millennium 先数出一千年，再指名千年交替的那一刻，最后经宗教文献引入「理想的黄金时代」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line of time divided into a thousand small squares.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被刻成一千个小格子的长长时间线。

branches.en: A thousand years counted together is the plain time span sense.
branches.cn: 把一千年数成一个整体，就是朴素的时段义项。

branches.en: The marked end of that span gives the turning-point sense.
branches.cn: 这一时段被标记的终点，给出了转折点的义项。

branches.en: Religious hope inflates the span into a perfect age.
branches.cn: 宗教希望把这段时光放大成完美的时代。

branches.en: A span and its opening moment are the same measure seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 一个时段与它的起始时刻，是同一把尺子的两面。

branches.en: Every turning point is greeted with promises of a better world.
branches.cn: 每个转折点都会被许诺一个更美好的世界。

intro.en: Millennium is a Latin compound of mille and annus, with the Latin noun suffix -ium and English derivatives around it.
intro.cn: millennium 是拉丁语 mille 与 annus 的合成词，带拉丁名词后缀 -ium，周围还有英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mille means a thousand and annus means a year.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mille 意为「一千」，annus 意为「年」。

items.example: Mille opens the word.
items.exampleCN: mille 是这个词的开头。

items.example: Annus closes the word.
items.exampleCN: annus 是这个词的末尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示事物或时期的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ium makes the compound a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ium 让这个合成词成为名词。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms millennial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 millennial。

items.example: Annual shows the annus stem alone.
items.exampleCN: annual 单独展示了 annus 这个词干。

items.example: Millimeter shows the same mille.
items.exampleCN: millimeter 展示了同一个 mille。

items.example: Century mirrors millennium at a smaller scale.
items.exampleCN: century 是 millennium 在小尺度上的对应。

items.example: Millennial keeps both roots visible.
items.exampleCN: millennial 同时呈现出两个词根。
